question:
In mathematical logic, which of the following are
statements?
(i) There will be snow in January.
(ii) What is the time now ?
(iii) Today is Sunday.
(iv) You must study Discrete Mathematics.
Choose the correct answer from the code given
below :
solution:
Option A is Correct
(i) There will be snow in January.
This is a declarative sentence. Although its truth
value depends on the context (e.g., location and
weather conditions), it can be classified as true or
false in a specific context. Hence, This is a
statement.
(ii) What is the time now?
This is a question and does not assert anything
that can be true or false. Hence, This is not a
statement.
(iii) Today is Sunday.
This is a declarative sentence that asserts
something about the day. Depending on the day,
it can be classified as true or false. Hence, This is
a statement.
(iv) You must study Discrete Mathematics.
This is a command or an advice, not a declarative
sentence. It cannot be classified as true or false.
Hence, This is not a statement.

question:
In PERT/CPM, the merge event represents ___ of
two or more events.
solution:
Option A is Correct
In PERT (Program Evaluation and Review
Technique) and CPM (Critical Path Method), a
merge event occurs when multiple preceding
activities converge at a single node. This implies
that all the activities leading to this node must be
completed for the merge event to occur.
Thus, in this context:
A merge event signals the completion of all
converging activities, enabling the next
activity or set of activities to start.
The merge event itself does not represent the
beginning of any specific activity; it simply
ensures that all incoming activities have been
finished.
A) Completion (Correct):
A merge event represents the completion of all
incoming activities, as all prerequisites must be
met before moving forward.

question:
Consider the following statements :
(i) Auto increment addressing mode is useful in
creating self-relocating code.
(ii) If auto increment addressing mode is included
in an instruction set architecture, then an
additional ALU is required for effective address
calculation.
(iii) In auto increment addressing mode, the
amount of increment depends on the size of the
data item accessed.
Which of the above statements is/are true?
Choose the correct answer from the code given
below :
solution:
Option C is Correct
Statement (i): Auto increment addressing mode is
useful in creating self-relocating code.
Auto increment addressing mode automatically
updates the address pointer after accessing a
memory location. This is useful in iterating
through arrays or data structures, but it does not
directly facilitate self-relocating code.
Self-relocating code refers to code that can
adjust itself to execute properly regardless of
where it is loaded in memory. Auto increment
addressing does not inherently assist in achieving
this.
Hence, This statement is false.
Statement (ii): If auto increment addressing mode
is included in an instruction set architecture, then
an additional ALU is required for effective
address calculation.
In auto increment addressing mode, the effective
address is calculated by adding a fixed or
variable increment to the current value of the
address pointer. This operation requires an
arithmetic addition.
An additional ALU may not always be required;
this depends on the hardware design. Many
processors reuse the existing ALU for both
effective address computation and general
arithmetic operations.
However, in some architectures, a separate unit
may be provided for this purpose.
Hence, This statement is not universally true and
is false for most modern architectures.
Statement (iii): In auto increment addressing
mode, the amount of increment depends on the
size of the data item accessed.
In most architectures, the auto increment amount
depends on the size of the data being accessed
(e.g., a 4-byte increment for a 32-bit integer or a
1-byte increment for a character).
This ensures that the next memory address
points to the subsequent data item.
Hence, This statement is true.

question:
The second smallest of n  elements can be found
with ____________ comparisons in the worst
case.
solution:
The correct option is C.
The second smallest element of n elements can
be found with n + ceil(log n )-2 comparisons in
the worst case.
If we have n elements, n-1 comparisons are
required to find the minimum element.
During the procedure, each element is compared
at most log n times. Because every time, we
compare the elements, at the second iteration
list, the search will proceed in n/2 elements. Then
in the next iteration, the search goes on for n/4
elements. In the end, there is only one element
left. So, at most log n times each element is
compared.
At the end, there are n + log n -2 comparisons to
find the second minimum element.

projection is/are true?

object is from the centre of projection, the

projection) appear smaller because the
projection rays converge at the center.

Q: In parallel projection, the projection rays are
parallel to one another, which means that the
projection direction is independent of the
object's position. This can be viewed as the
spectator being infinitely far away so that the
convergence of projection beams (as in
perspective projection) is unimportant and the
rays are actually parallel.

solution:
The dirty bit is a flag in the page table entry of a
memory management system.
It is used to indicate whether a page in memory
has been modified (written to) after it was
loaded from disk into memory.
If the dirty bit is set (value = 1), it means the page
has been modified and must be written back to
the disk before being replaced or removed from
memory.
If the dirty bit is not set (value = 0), it means the
page has not been modified, and there is no
need to write it back to disk when it is removed.
Purpose of the Dirty Bit:
It improves efficiency in memory management
because it avoids unnecessary writes to disk for
pages that haven't been modified.
It is commonly used in virtual memory systems
and caching mechanisms.
Option D is correct.

question:
A basic feasible solution of an 
transportation problem is said to be non-
degenerate, if basic feasible solution contains
exactly------------- number of individual allocation
in-------------- positions.
solution:
Transportation Problem:
A transportation problem is a special type of
linear programming problem.
The goal is to minimize the transportation cost
while satisfying supply and demand constraints.
Feasible Solution:
A feasible solution satisfies all supply and
demand constraints.
A basic feasible solution is a feasible solution
that corresponds to a set of independent
allocations (non-zero variables in the solution
matrix).
Number of Allocations in Basic Feasible
Solution:
For a transportation problem with m rows
(supplies) and n columns (demands), the basic
feasible solution: m+n−1 allocations (non-zero
values).
This is because the number of independent
constraints is m+n−1, ensuring no degeneracy in
the solution.
Non-Degeneracy:
A solution is non-degenerate if it has m+n−1
independent allocations.
If the number of allocations is fewer than m+n−1,
the solution is degenerate.
Final Answer:
B. m+n−1, independent

question:
Let (P) be the set of all people. Let (R) be a binary
relation on (P) such that (a, b) is in R if a is a
brother of b. Is (R) symmetric transitive, an
equivalence relation, a partial order relation?
solution:
1. Symmetry
A relation R is symmetric if (a,b)∈R⟹(b,a)∈R.
If a is a brother of b, it does not necessarily
mean that b is a brother of a. For example, if b
is a sister, then b is not a "brother."
R is not symmetric.
2. Transitivity
A relation R is transitive if (a,b)∈R and
(b,c)∈R⟹(a,c)∈R.
If a is a brother of b, and b is a brother of c,
then a will also be a brother of c.
R is transitive.
3. Equivalence Relation
A relation is an equivalence relation if it is
reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.
Reflexivity: (a,a)∈R  A person cannot be their
own brother, so R is not reflexive.
Symmetry: R is not symmetric.
Transitivity: R is transitive.
Since R is not reflexive or symmetric, it is not an
equivalence relation.
4. Partial Order Relation
A relation is a partial order if it is reflexive,
antisymmetric, and transitive.
Reflexivity: R is not reflexive
Antisymmetry: R is antisymmetric if (a,b)∈R
and (b,a)∈R⟹a=b.R is not antisymmetric, as
two distinct brothers a and b can satisfy
(a,b)∈R and (b,a)∈R.
Transitivity: R is transitive.
Since R is not reflexive or antisymmetric, it is not
a partial order relation.
Option C is correct.

field which is divided into 2 subfields F1 and F2,

condition field CD for four status bits, branch

).

Option A is correct.

question:
Which of the following methods are used to pass
any number of parameters to the operating
system through system calls?

options.B: Block or table in main memory
options.D: Block in main memory and stack

solution:
Explanation:
When a program makes a system call, it needs a
way to send information to the operating system.
These are used to pass the parameters as below:
1. Using Register - It is stored directly in the CPU
Register, It is very fast but can only handle a
limited number of parameters due to the limited
number of registers.
2. Using a Block in Memory: It is stored in a
designated block of memory, and the address of
this block is passed to the Operating System
through a register. 
3. Using Stack: It is pushed onto the program's
stack, and the Operating System retrieves them
when processing the system call.
i.e., we can say that the method used to pass any
number of parameters to the operating system
through system calls is by using a block in
memory and the stack.
The Final Answer is: Block in main memory and
stack

question:
Consider the following statements with respect
to duality in LPP :
(a) The final simplex table giving optimal solution
of the primal also contains optimal solution of its
dual in itself.
(b) If either the primal or the dual problem has a
finite optimal solution, then the other problem
also has a finite optimal solution.
(c) If either problem has an unbounded optimum
solution, then the other problem has no feasible
solution at all.
Which of the statements is (are) correct?
solution:
The correct option is D.
Duality in Linear programming problem has
another LPP which is derived from it. Original LPP
is known as primal and derived LPP is known as
Dual.
Some points about dual LPP:
1) The final simplex table giving the optimal
solution of the primal also contains the optimal
solution of its dual in itself.
2) If either the primal or the dual problem has a
finite optimal solution, then the other problem
also has a finite optimal solution.
3) If either problem has an unbounded optimum
solution, then the other problem has no feasible
solution at all.

question:

characteristics are :
(a) Single cycle instruction execution
(b) Variable length instruction formats
(c) Instructions that manipulates operands in
memory
(d) Efficient instruction pipeline
Choose the correct characteristics from the
options given below :
solution:
The correct option is C.
Statement A is correct: RISC has pipelined
implementations with the goal of executing one
instruction per machine cycle.
Statement B is incorrect: RISC has fixed-length
instruction formats.
Statement C is incorrect: RISC can perform only
Register to Register Arithmetic operations.
Statement D is correct: RISC has efficient
instruction pipeline. 
So, only statements a and d are correct.

to approaches to fill areas on raster systems :
P: To determine the overlap intervals for scan
lines that cross the area.
Q ：  To start from a given interior position and
paint outward from this point until we encounter
the specified boundary conditions.

below :
solution:
The correct option is C.
There are two approaches used in the area filling
on raster systems: one is the scan line algorithm
and another is the seed fill algorithm.
1) Scan line algorithm: It determines the overlap
intervals for scan lines that cross the area or scan

the display area horizontally.

position and points outward from this point until
the boundary condition is reached. In this, a point
is selected and then four or eight connected
approaches is used to fill it.

question:
Two concurrent executing transactions  and 
 are allowed to update same stock item say ' A
' in an uncontrolled manner. In such scenario,
following problems may occur :
(a) Dirty read problem
(b) Lost update problem
(c) Transaction failure
(d) Inconsistent database state
Which of the following option is correct if
database system has no concurrency module and
allows concurrent execution of above two
transactions?
solution:
The correct option is D.
Problems that can occur during the concurrent
execution of two transactions in an uncontrolled
manner.
a) Lost update problem: A lost update problem
occurs when two transactions that access the
same database items have their operations
interleaved in a way that makes the value of
some database item incorrect.
b) Dirty read problem: It occurs when a
transaction is allowed to retrieve or update a
record that has been updated by another
transaction. Because it has not yet been
committed, there is always a possibility that it will
never be committed but rather roll back.
d) Inconsistent database state: It occurs when a
transaction reads several values but a second
transaction updates some of these values during
the execution of the first. This causes an
inconsistency.

question:
Identify the circumstances under which pre-
emptive CPU scheduling is used :
(a) A process switches from Running state to
Ready state
(b) A process switches from Waiting state to
Ready state
(c) A process completes its execution
(d) A process switches from Ready to Waiting
state
Choose the correct option :
solution:
The correct option is A.
 CPU scheduling decisions take place under one
of four conditions:
1. When a process switches from the running
state to the waiting state, such as for an I/O
request or invocation of the wait( ) system call.
2. When a process switches from the running
state to the ready state, for example in response
      |       |   


UGC	NET
to an interrupt.
3. When a process switches from the waiting
state to the ready state, say at completion of I/O
or a return from wait( ).
4. When a process terminates.
For conditions 1 and 4 there is no choice - A new
process must be selected.
For conditions 2 and 3 there is a choice - To
either continue running the current process, or
select a different one.
If scheduling takes place only under conditions 1
and 4, the system is said to be non-preemptive,
or cooperative. Under these conditions, once a
process starts running it keeps running, until it
either voluntarily blocks or until it finishes.
Otherwise, the system is said to be preemptive.
In above discussion. it's given that If scheduling
takes place only under conditions 1 and 4, the
system is said to be non-preemptive. Otherwise,
the system is said to be preemptive.
Therefore point 2 & 3 are condition for
preemptive system. Here point 2 and 3 are as
listed below When a process switches from the
running state to the ready state. When a process
switches from the waiting state to the ready
state.
These above point matches with circumstances
(a) & (b) given in question.

question:

(a) Fiber optic cable is much lighter than copper
cable.
(b) Fiber optic cable is not affected by power
surges or electromagnetic interference.
(c) Optical transmission is inherently bidirectional.
Which of the statements is (are) correct?

cables. Also, fibre optic cable have higher

signal is not affected by electrical noise.

This statement is incorrect. Two optical modules
are connected by a single fibre cable which
supports unidirectional communication. For bi-
directional communication, two cables will be
required.

question:
Consider the following statements with respect
to network security :
(a) Message confidentiality means that the
sender and the receiver expect privacy.
(b) Message integrity means that the data must
arrive at the receiver exactly as they were sent.
(c) Message authentication means the receiver is
ensured that the message is coming from the
intended sender.
Which of the statements is (are) correct?
solution:

Message Confidentiality- It means a set of
rules and promises that are executed through
confidentiality agreements.

must not be modified in  transit.

that the message is not changed and also the

question:
Consider the following:
(a) Trapping at local maxima
(b) Reaching a plateau
(c) Traversal along the ridge.
Which of the following option represents
shortcomings of the hill climbing algorithm?
solution:
The correct option is D.
Problems in hill climbing are: 
1) Local maximum: It is a state that is better than
all of its neighbors but is not better than some
other states that are farther away. The solution of
this problem is backtracking. 
2) Plateau: It is a flat area of search space in
which a whole set of neighbouring states have
the same value. On a plateau, it is not possible to
determine the best direction in which to move. 
3) Ridge: It is an area of search space which is
higher than the surrounding areas and that itself
has a slope.

question:
Consider the following learning algorithms :
(a) Logistic repression
(b) Back propogation
(c) Linear repression
Which of the following option represents
classification algorithms?
solution:
Option A is correct
Logistic Regression:
Logistic regression is a classification algorithm
used to predict discrete outcomes (e.g., binary
classes such as 0/1, spam/not spam). It uses a
logistic function (sigmoid) to map predictions to
probabilities. Hence, it can be categorised as
Classification algorithm.
Backpropagation:
Backpropagation is a learning algorithm used in
training neural networks. Neural networks are
versatile and can be used for both classification
and regression tasks. It is a Classification
algorithm when applied to classification
problems (e.g., image recognition).
Linear Regression:
Linear regression is a regression algorithm used
to predict continuous outcomes (e.g., house
prices, temperature). It fits a linear relationship
between input variables and the output. Hence,
It is Not a classification algorithm.

question:
Given six weights 4,15,25,5,8,16 construct a
 tree. What is the minimum weighted path
length?
solution:
Option B is Correct
To solve this problem, a 2-tree (Huffman Tree) is
constructed using the given weights, and the
minimum weighted path length is calculated. In a
Huffman Tree, it is necessary to repeatedly
combine the two smallest weights until only one
node remains.
Here, the weights are 4, 15, 25, 5, 8, 16
Steps to Build the Huffman Tree
1. Sort the weights in ascending order: 4, 5, 8, 15,
16, 25
2. Combine the two smallest weights repeatedly
and keep track of the sum at each step. Each
combined weight represents an internal node
in the tree, and the total path length is the
sum of these weights at different depths.
Step-by-Step Construction
Combine 4 and 5 → 4 + 5 = 9
New list: 8, 9, 15, 16, 25
Combine 8 and 9 → 8 + 9 = 17
New list: 15, 16, 17, 25
Combine 15 and 16 → 15 + 16 = 31
New list: 17, 25, 31
Combine 17 and 25 → 17 + 25 = 42
New list: 31, 42
Combine 31 and 42 → 31 + 42 = 73
New list: 73
Now, we sum all intermediate weights used in
combining to calculate the weighted path length:
9 + 17 + 31 + 42 + 73 = 172
The minimum weighted path length is 172.

question:
What is the minimum Hamming Distance in a
block code if we want to be able to detect up to
(S) errors?
solution:
The Hamming distance between two code words
(pieces of data) is simply the number of bit
positions in which they differ. For example, if two
binary numbers have a Hamming distance of 3, it
means three bits are different between them.
Error detection:
1. If we want to detect up to S errors (meaning
there could be S incorrect bits in the data), we
need the minimum Hamming distance
between any two valid code words to be S + 1.
2. If two valid code words differ by S + 1 bits,
then even if S bits change (due to errors), the
received word will still not match another valid
code word. This allows detect that an error has
occurred.
The correct option is B.

question:
Which search technique is complete and optimal,
when   is consistent?
solution:
A search algorithm is complete if it guarantees
finding a solution if one exists.
A search algorithm is optimal if it finds the least-
cost solution.
A heuristic function h(n) is consistent if, for every
node n and every successor n′ of n generated by
any action a, the following inequality holds: h(n) ≤
c(n,n′)+h(n′) where c(n,n′) is the cost of reaching n′
from n. This property is known as the
monotonicity property.
A* Search:  Search is known to be both complete
and optimal when the heuristic h(n) is consistent.
Option C is correct.

question:

process as a single inference rule?
solution:
C) Generalized Modus Ponens is an inference
rule used in logic and artificial intelligence that
extends the basic modus ponens rule. Modus
ponens is a simple rule of inference that states:
If "P implies Q" (P → Q) is true and P is true, then

question: Fuzzy logic is a form of ____
solution:
D) Many valued logic
Correct: Fuzzy logic is a form of many-valued
logic that allows for values between true and
false, rather than the binary choices of true (1) or
false (0). Fuzzy logic can handle partial truth,
where values can range continuously between
completely true and completely false.
For example, in fuzzy logic, a statement like "The
weather is warm" could have a truth value of 0.7,
representing that it is somewhat true, rather than
strictly true or false. This flexibility is particularly
useful in systems that deal with uncertainty, like
control systems and decision-making processes
in artificial intelligence.

defining and understanding the problem before
moving on to data collection, modeling, and
evaluation.

question:
Which of the following statement is/are True?
A. The processor has direct access to both
primary and secondary memory
B. Primary memory stores the active instructions
and data for the program being executed on the
process
C. Secondary memory is used as a backup
memory
D. Memory system is implemented on a single
level memory
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Statement A: "The processor has direct access
to both primary and secondary memory."
False. The processor has direct access to primary
memory (RAM), where active instructions and
data are stored for quick access during
execution. However, it does not have direct
access to secondary memory (such as hard
drives or SSDs).
Statement B: "Primary memory stores the
active instructions and data for the program
being executed on the processor."
True. Primary memory (RAM) holds the active
data and instructions that the processor needs to
execute programs. This is the main purpose of
primary memory, providing fast access to the
processor.
Statement C: "Secondary memory is used as a
backup memory."
True. Secondary memory, such as hard drives,
SSDs, or external storage, is used for long-term
storage and acts as a backup to primary memory.
It retains data even when the system is powered
off.
Statement D: "Memory system is implemented
on a single level memory."
False. Modern computer systems use a multi-
level memory system, which includes primary
memory (RAM), secondary memory (hard drives,
SSDs), and often cache memory. This multi-level
approach helps optimize speed and storage
capacity.
Option B is correct answer.

question:
Inheritance provides the benefits of 
A. shared interfaces
B. run-time polymorphism
C. less redundant information
D. dynamic binding
Choose the Correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Inheritance in object-oriented programming
provides the following benefits:
Run-time Polymorphism (B):
True. Inheritance enables run-time
polymorphism, which allows derived classes to
override methods of the base class. This is
achieved through dynamic method, allowing
different implementations to be called based on
the object's runtime type.
Less Redundant Information (C):
True. Inheritance helps reduce redundancy by
allowing derived classes to reuse the attributes
and behaviors (methods) of a base class. This
means that shared code does not need to be
duplicated across multiple classes.
Dynamic Binding (D):
True. Inheritance supports dynamic binding,
where method calls are resolved at runtime
rather than compile-time. This enables
polymorphism and allows derived classes to
provide specific implementations of methods
defined in the base class.
Correct option is C.

question:
Which of the following statements are true?
A. If the time quantum is extremely small, round
robin can result in a large number of context
switches.
B. The average turnaround time of a set of
processes does not necessarily improve as the
time-quantum size increases.
C. The average turnaround time can be improved
if most processes finish their next CPU burst in a
single time quantum.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Statement A: "If the time quantum is extremely
small, round robin can result in a large number
of context switches."
True. In Round Robin scheduling, each process is
given a small amount of CPU time (time
quantum) before switching to the next process. If
the time quantum is too small, the CPU will
frequently switch between processes, resulting in
a large number of context switches. This can lead
to overhead and inefficiency.
Statement B: "The average turnaround time of
a set of processes does not necessarily improve
as the time-quantum size increases."
True. Increasing the time quantum does not
always lead to a lower average turnaround time.
If the time quantum is too large, Round Robin
effectively behaves like a First-Come, First-
Served (FCFS) scheduling algorithm, which might
not provide a good average turnaround time.
Statement C: "The average turnaround time can
be improved if most processes finish their next
CPU burst in a single time quantum."

allows most processes to complete their CPU
bursts within a single quantum, the system can
reduce waiting times and context switches,
improving the average turnaround time.

solution:
The basic page replacement process follows
these steps in order:
C. Location of desired frame is found from disk:
This step happens first for finding the location of
the page to be replaced. In some systems, the
operating system may first locate the desired
page (or the page to be swapped in) on disk
before taking any other action.
A. Page replacement algorithm is used in case
there is no free frame:
After finding the desired page on disk, the page
replacement algorithm is invoked to decide
which page in memory will be replaced if there
are no free frames available. This happens when
there's a page fault.
D. Desired page is brought into newly freed
frame and page & frame tables are updated:
Once the replacement page is identified, the
desired page is loaded into the newly freed
frame, and the relevant page and frame tables
are updated to reflect this change.
B. The process is continued by restarting the
instruction caused by TRAP:

question:
Which of the following rotations are correctly
explained in the context of an AVL tree.
A. LL rotation: The new node is inserted in the
left sub-tree of the left sub-tree of the critical
node.
B. RR rotation: The new node is inserted in the
right sub-tree of the right sub-tree of the critical
node.
C. LR rotation: The new node is inserted in the
right sub-tree of the left sub-tree of the critical
node.
D. RL rotation: The new node is inserted in the
left sub-tree of the right sub-tree of the critical
node
      |       |
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
In an AVL tree, rotations are performed to
maintain balance when a new node is inserted,
causing the tree to become unbalanced. Each
type of rotation corresponds to a specific
insertion scenario:
LL Rotation: The new node is inserted in the left
sub-tree of the left sub-tree of the critical node.
Correct because an LL imbalance occurs when a
node is added to the left sub-tree of the left
child, causing a left-heavy imbalance.
RR Rotation: The new node is inserted in the
right sub-tree of the right sub-tree of the critical
node.
Correct because an RR imbalance occurs when a
node is added to the right sub-tree of the right
child, causing a right-heavy imbalance.
LR Rotation: The new node is inserted in the
right sub-tree of the left sub-tree of the critical
node.
Correct because an LR imbalance occurs when a
node is added to the right sub-tree of the left
child, requiring a left-right rotation to balance the
tree.
RL Rotation: The new node is inserted in the left
sub-tree of the right sub-tree of the critical node.
Correct because an RL imbalance occurs when a
node is added to the left sub-tree of the right
child, requiring a right-left rotation to balance the
tree.

question:
Which of the following statement(s) are correct?
A. Syntax Directed Translation can be applied in
Type Checking.
B. Syntax Directed Translation can be used in 3-
address code generation.
C. Syntax Directed Translation can be used in
construction of syntax tree.
D. Syntax Directed Translation can be used to
recognize valid tokens.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
solution:
Option A is Correct
Option A: Syntax Directed Translation can be
applied in Type Checking.
It is Correct as SDT can indeed be used in type
checking. Semantic rules attached to grammar
productions can perform type checks on the
attributes of syntactic constructs. For example, in
a compiler, SDT can verify that an operation
between variables respects type compatibility
rules.
Option B: Syntax Directed Translation can be
used in 3-address code generation.
It is Correct as SDT is commonly used in
generating intermediate representations, such as
3-address code, by associating actions that
produce the code with grammar productions.
This is a key use of SDT in compiler construction.
Option C: Syntax Directed Translation can be
used in the construction of a syntax tree.
It is Correct as SDT can be used to build syntax
trees by associating actions with grammar
productions that construct tree nodes. This is
part of semantic analysis in compilers, where
syntax trees represent the hierarchical structure
of source code.
Option D: Syntax Directed Translation can be
used to recognize valid tokens.
It is Incorrect as Token recognition is typically
handled by the lexical analyzer (lexer), which
operates before syntax analysis. SDT is applied
during and after parsing (syntax analysis) and is
not responsible for recognizing tokens. SDT
focuses on attaching semantic actions to
grammar productions rather than tokenizing
input, which is outside its scope.

question:

networks.

which the data set is very large.
C. They are able to extract features without input
from the programmer.

learning algorithm inspired by the structure and
function of the human brain. They are widely
used in supervised, unsupervised, and
reinforcement learning tasks.
Statement B: "It is useful when solving the
problems for which the data set is very large."
Correct. Neural networks, especially deep neural
networks, excel in processing large datasets and
are particularly effective in applications such as
image recognition, natural language processing,
and other areas that require large volumes of
data.

without input from the programmer."

learning, can automatically learn features from
data during the training process. This is known as
feature extraction, where the network identifies
patterns and hierarchies in the data without
explicit programming.
Statement D: "These are systems modeled on
the human brain and nervous system."
Correct. Neural networks are inspired by the
structure of the human brain, with layers of
neurons (nodes) that simulate the brain’s ability
to recognize patterns and make decisions.
The correct option is D.

A. Timestamp protocol: The timestamp protocol
is a concurrency control mechanism that assigns
a unique timestamp to each transaction. The
main feature of this protocol is that it ensures
transactions are executed based on their
timestamps, which helps maintain consistency
without locking resources. If a transaction
attempts to access data that has been modified
by another transaction with an earlier timestamp,
it will be rolled back or delayed. This approach
also prevents deadlock situations.
B. Strict two-phase locking protocol: Strict two-
phase locking (S2PL) is a locking protocol where
all locks are acquired before any locks are
released. This guarantees serializability and
prevents cascading rollbacks but can lead to
deadlocks if not managed properly.
C. Two-phase locking: Two-phase locking (2PL)
is a concurrency control method that requires
transactions to acquire all necessary locks before
releasing any. It consists of two phases: the
growing phase (where locks are acquired) and
the shrinking phase (where locks are released).
While it ensures serializability, it does not prevent
deadlocks.
D. Lock point in two-phase locking protocol:
The lock point refers to the moment in time when
a transaction acquires its last lock during its
execution. In 2PL, this point is crucial because it
determines when other transactions can see
changes made by this transaction.

question:
Let ' G ' be a simple, undirected graph with n
(n>10) vertices and k connected components.
What is the minimum possible number of edges
of G?
solution:
The correct answer is option D.
A connected component in a graph is a subset of
the graph where there is a path between any two
vertices within that subset, and no vertex in the
subset is connected to any vertex outside it.
Step 1: Minimum Edges for Each Component
For each connected component, at least one
edge is required to connect two vertices.
However, if we want to minimize the number of
edges while still maintaining connectivity within
each component, we can use trees as our
structure. A tree is a type of graph that is
minimally connected; it has exactly v−1 edges for
v vertices. Thus, for each connected component
containing n vertices (where i =1,2,...,k),
The minimum number of edges needed to keep
that component connected is: n−1
Step 2: Total Vertices and Components
Since we have n total vertices distributed across
k components, we can express this as:
n+n+...+n=n
Step 3: Calculating Minimum Edges for All
Components
The total minimum number of edges required for
all k components would be:
(n−1)+(n−1)+...+(n−1)
= (n+n+...+n)−k=n−k
Therefore, the minimum possible number of
edges in a simple undirected graph with n
vertices and k connected components are n-k

Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm

At Timestamp t2:

The C_LOOK algorithm services the requests in a

question:

Consider the following statements about
the given query that retrieves the set of all
students whose gender is same as the
gender of their advisor:
S1. It has a correlated subquery
S2. It has an uncorrelated subquery
S3. If we replace ALL by ANY in the above
query, its result will be different
S4. If we replace ALL by ANY in the above
query, its result will be same.
Identify all the statement that are TRUE:
solution:
The correct answer is option A.
Given Query:
SELECT s.rollno 
FROM student s 
WHERE s.sex = ALL (SELECT f.sex FROM professor
f WHERE f.empid = s.advisor)

True: S1 It has a correlated subquery.
The subquery (SELECT f.sex FROM professor f

the outer query, making it correlated.
False: S2 It has an uncorrelated subquery.

subquery would not reference any columns from

True: S3 If we replace ALL with ANY in the above

lead to different results. ANY checks if the
condition is true for at least one value, while ALL

question:
Which one of the following types of memory is
the fastest?
solution:
Option A: Cache memory is a small, fast memory
unit located close to the CPU. It stores frequently
used data and instructions that have been
recently accessed from the main memory.
Option B: Registers are small, high-speed
memory units located in the CPU. They are used
to store the most frequently used data and
instructions. Registers have the fastest access
time and the smallest storage capacity.
Option C: Main memory, also known as RAM
(Random Access Memory), is the primary
memory of a computer system. It has a larger
storage capacity than cache memory, but it is
slower.
Option D: Secondary storage, such as hard disk
drives (HDD) and solid-state drives (SSD), is a
non-volatile memory unit that has a larger
storage capacity than main memory. 
So option B is the correct answer.

question:
Consider an unpipelined machine with 10 nsec
clock cycles which uses four cycles for ALU
operations and branches where as five cycles for
memory operation. Assume that the relative
frequencies of these operations are: 40 %, 20 %
and 40 %, respectively. Due to clock skew and
setup pipeline let us consider that the machine
adds one nsec overhead to the clock. How much
speedup is observed in the instruction execution
rate when a pipelined machine is considered?
solution:
To calculate the speedup observed in the
instruction execution rate when a pipelined
machine is considered, let's first analyze the
unpipelined machine.
In the unpipelined machine:
ALU operations take 4 clock cycles (40% of
the time).
Branch operations take 4 clock cycles (20% of
the time)
Memory operations take 5 clock cycles (40%
of the time).
Total clock cycle =0.40 * 4+0.20 * 4+0.40 * 5
Total Clock Cycle =1.6+0.8+2
Total Clock Cycle = 4.4 Clock Cycle
Here,
Without using pipeline processor one instruction
takes  =4.4 clock cycle * 10 nsec  =44 nsec
Pipeline time = Clock time + overhead time =10
nsec+1 nsec=11 nsec (Clock cycle time is 10 ns
with an additional 1 ns overhead, making it 11 ns
per cycle.)
Speedup= Time taken by non-pipeline machine /
Time taken by pipeline machine
Speedup =44 / 11=4
So option B is the correct answer.

specific task at the hardware level, such as
arithmetic or logical operations, data movement,
or control flow.

solution:
Option A: The number is always positive when
the qualifier 'unsigned' is used. This is correct.
When a variable is declared as 'unsigned', it
means that it can only represent non-negative
values, including zero. This is because the sign bit
is not reserved, and all bits in the variable's
memory representation are used to represent the
magnitude of the value. So, unsigned variables
can only hold positive values or zero.
Option B: The number can be positive or
negative when the qualifier 'signed' is used.
This is correct. When a variable is declared as
'signed', it means that it can represent both
positive and negative values. The variable
reserves one bit for the sign, usually the leftmost
bit (the most significant bit). If this bit is 0, the
number is positive, and if it's 1, the number is
negative. The rest of the bits represent the
magnitude of the value.
Option C: The range of values for signed data
types is more than that of unsigned data types.
This statement is incorrect. The range of values
for signed data types is typically less than that of
unsigned data types. For example, an 8-bit
unsigned data type can represent values from 0
to 255, whereas an 8-bit signed data type can

in signed data types, one bit is used to represent

statement is correct because unsigned numbers
do not preserve a bit for a sign, so all the bits are
used to represent the value of the number.

question:
The main function of the microkernel is to
provide a communication facility between the
__________program and the various _____ that
are also running in user space.
solution:
In the mid-1980s, researchers at Carnegie Mellon
University developed an operating system called
Mach that modularized the kernel using the
microkernel approach.
• This method structures the operating system by
removing all nonessential components from the
kernel and implementing them as system and
user-level programs.
• Microkernel provides minimal process and
memory management, in addition to a
communication facility.
• The main function of the microkernel is to
provide communication between the client
program and the various services that are also
running in user space.
• The client program and service never interact
directly. Rather, they communicate indirectly by
exchanging messages with the microkernel.
• One benefit of the microkernel approach is that
it makes extending the operating system easier.
All new services are added to user space and
consequently do not require modification of the
kernel. 
So option C is the correct answer.

question:
Modifying the software to match changes in the
ever-changing environment is called as
solution:
Software maintenance refers to the process of
modifying, updating, and managing software
after it has been deployed. It encompasses all
activities involved in keeping a software system
operational, up-to-date, and aligned with
changing requirements and environments
throughout its lifecycle. Software maintenance
typically includes several key activities:
Option A:  Adaptive maintenance- Adaptive
maintenance involves modifying the software
to adapt it to changes in the environment, such
as operating system upgrades, hardware
changes, or new regulations. The goal is to
ensure that the software remains compatible
and effective in its operating environment.
Option B: Corrective maintenance- This involves
fixing defects or bugs in the software identified
during its use. Corrective maintenance aims to
address issues that affect the performance,
reliability, or functionality of the software.
Option C: Perfective maintenance-Perfective
maintenance focuses on improving the software's
performance, efficiency, and user experience. It
includes enhancements that add new features,
optimize existing functionality, or improve the
software's usability based on user feedback.
Option D: Preventive maintenance- Preventive
maintenance aims to proactively identify and
address potential issues before they impact the
software's performance or stability. It involves
activities such as code refactoring, performance
tuning, and security audits to prevent future
problems.
So Modifying the software to match changes in
the ever-changing environment is called option
A, Adaptive maintenance.

question:
Given the FFT we can have ______ time
procedure for multiplying two polynomials A(x)
and B(x) of degree bound n where input and
output representations are in coefficient form,
assuming n is a power of 2.
solution:
Representation Conversion: First, the polynomials
A(x) and B(x) are converted from coefficient form
to point-value form. This involves evaluating both
polynomials at certain points, typically using
roots of unity. This step can be done in O(n) time.
FFT Computation: Once the polynomials are in
point-value form, the FFT algorithm is applied to
each polynomial separately. The Cooley-Tukey
FFT algorithm is commonly used, which has a
time complexity of O(n log n) for polynomials of
size n, where n is a power of 2.
Pointwise Multiplication: After computing the FFT
of each polynomial, the coefficients are
multiplied pointwise. This operation has a time
complexity of O(n) since there are n coefficients
to multiply.
Inverse FFT: Finally, the result of the pointwise
multiplication is transformed back to coefficient
form using the inverse FFT. Similar to the forward
FFT, the inverse FFT also has a time complexity of
O(nlogn).
So option B is the correct answer.

integer p ≥ 1, that depends only on L, such that
for every string w in L of length greater than or

portion of the string is known as pumping.

question: The A* algorithm is optimal when,

options.A:
It always finds the solution with the lowest
total cost if the heuristic 'h' is admissible.
options.B:
Always finds the solution with the highest
total cost if the heuristic 'h' is admissible.
options.C:
Finds the solution with the lowest total cost if
the heuristic 'h' is not admissible.
options.D:
It always finds the solution with the highest
total cost if the heuristic 'h' is not admissible.

solution:
A* problem: Given a network of nodes such that
the links between nodes have costs associated
with them, find the least expensive path from a
starting node to a goal node.  (For example,
nodes could be cities and link distances.)  A*
search is an optimal algorithm in that it is
guaranteed to find the shortest path if one exists.
 In addition, A* will be optimally efficient. That is,
no other optimal algorithm is guaranteed to
expand fewer nodes than A* search.
In A* search, node n is expanded with a priority
equal to f(n), such that in each cycle of the
algorithm, the node with the lowest f(n) value is
first expanded, and then removed from the
queue.  The function f(n) is
f(n) = g(n) + h(n)
where g(n) is the distance from the start node to
node n, and h(n) is a heuristic estimate of the
distance from node n to a goal node. If h(n) is
always an underestimate of the actual distance
from node n to the nearest goal node, then the
function h is said to be an admissible heuristic
function, and A*’s guarantee of optimal efficiency
will hold.
So option A is the correct answer.

question:
Where does the values of alpha-beta search get
updated?
solution:
One optimization method for the minimax
algorithm is alpha-beta pruning. It greatly cuts
down on computation time. As a result, we may
search the game tree considerably more quickly
and even reach deeper levels. It removes game
tree branches that don't need to be explored
because there is already a better move available.
Because it feeds two additional parameters—
alpha and beta—into the minimax algorithm, it is
known as "Alpha-Beta pruning."
The best value the algorithm can promise at that
level or higher is called alpha, and the best value
it can guarantee at that level or lower is called
beta. Alpha and beta are updated continuously
as the algorithm searches through the game tree,
thereby supplying upper bounds on the values
that can be retrieved by the tree's remaining
unanalyzed portions. This makes it possible to
prune branches that have no chance of
influencing the outcome, increasing the
algorithm's efficiency.
Alpha and beta values, which are normally
initialized to negative and positive infinity,
respectively, are introduced in the initial state.
Although the end state does offer precise alpha-
beta values, these are changed during the search
process rather than at the conclusion. So option
A is the correct answer.

Consider the following statements:
A. There exists a Boolean algebra with ' 5 '
elements.
B. Every element of Boolean algebra has a
unique complement.
C. If a Lattice ' L ' is a Boolean algebra then ' L ' is
not relatively complemented.
D. The direct product of two Boolean Algebras is
also a Boolean algebra.
Choose the correct answer about the four
statements given above.

options.A: Only A and D are correct
options.B: Only B and D are correct

solution:
A. There exists a Boolean algebra with ' 5 '
elements.
This is not true. Since a Boolean algebra is made
up of all subsets of a set of size n, it has 2
elements, where n is a positive integer. Since 5 is
not a power of 2, it cannot be a Boolean algebra
if it has 5 elements.
B. Every element of Boolean algebra has a
unique complement.
This statement is true. In a Boolean algebra, each
element has a unique complement, which is
another element that, when combined with the
original element using the Boolean operations
(AND, OR, NOT), results in the identity element (0
for OR, 1 for AND).
C. If a Lattice ' L ' is a Boolean algebra then ' L ' is
not relatively complemented.
This is not true. If there is an element b such that
a  b=0 and a  b=1for every element a, then
the lattice L 'is said to be complemented. These
components are referred to as each other's
complements. The lattice is referred to as
relatively complemented if these complements
are unique. A Boolean algebra is a particular type
of lattice in which every element has a unique
complement. In other words, 'L' is reasonably
complemented if it is a Boolean algebra.
D. The direct product of two Boolean Algebras is
also a Boolean algebra.
This statement is true. The direct product of two
Boolean algebras is defined as the Cartesian
product of their underlying sets equipped with
component-wise Boolean operations. The
resulting structure satisfies all the properties of a
Boolean algebra.
So option B is the correct answer.

question:
Which of the following is/are true for Dynamic
RAM (DRAM)?
1. It is slower than static RAM(SRAM)
2. Packing Density is higher than Static RAM
(SRAM)
3. It is faster than static RAM(SRAM)
4. It requires data refreshing
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
1. It is slower than static RAM (SRAM):
This statement is true. DRAM is generally slower
than SRAM because it requires periodic
refreshing to maintain data, which adds overhead
to access times. SRAM, on the other hand, does
not require refreshing and typically has faster
access times.
2. Packing Density is higher than Static RAM
(SRAM):
This statement is true. DRAM typically has a
higher packing density than SRAM because it
stores each bit as a charge on a capacitor, which
requires fewer components compared to the flip-
flop design used in SRAM. As a result, DRAM can
store more data in the same physical space.
3. It is faster than static RAM (SRAM):
This statement is false. As mentioned earlier,
DRAM is generally slower than SRAM due to the
need for periodic refreshing. SRAM has faster
access times because it uses flip-flops to store
data, which retains data as long as power is
supplied without the need for refreshing.
4. It requires data refreshing:
This statement is true. DRAM requires periodic
refreshing to maintain the charge on its
capacitors, which represent the stored data.
Without refreshing, the charge on the capacitors
would gradually leak away, resulting in data loss.
So option A is the correct answer.

question:
What are the drawbacks of using file systems to
store data?
1. Data inconsistency
2. Difficulty in accessing data
3. Data isolation
4. Atomicity of updates
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Data inconsistency:
File systems do not inherently enforce data
consistency. Concurrent access to files by
multiple processes or users can lead to data
inconsistency issues if proper synchronization
mechanisms are not implemented. For example, if
one process is writing to a file while another
process is reading from it, the reading process
might encounter inconsistent or partially
updated data.
Difficulty in accessing data:
File systems typically organize data into
hierarchical structures (directories and files),
which may result in difficulty accessing data
efficiently, especially when dealing with large
volumes of data. Locating specific files or
navigating through directory structures can
become cumbersome, particularly in complex file
systems.
Data isolation:
File systems lack built-in mechanisms for
enforcing data isolation, which can lead to
unintended access or modification of data by
unauthorized users or processes. Without proper
access controls and permissions, sensitive data
stored in files may be vulnerable to unauthorized
access or tampering.
Atomicity of updates:
File systems do not guarantee the atomicity of
updates, meaning that modifications to files or
directories may not be performed as a single,
indivisible operation. If a failure occurs during a
file modification operation (e.g., writing data to a
file), it may result in partial updates, leaving the
file in an inconsistent or corrupted state.
So option D is the correct answer.

organized into a tree-like structure where each
record consists of one parent record and many
children. In the hierarchical model, segments
pointed to by the logical association are called
the child segment and the other segment is
called the parent segment. If there is a segment
without a parent then that will be called the root
and the segment that has no children is called
the leaves. 
2. In a network database model, data is
organized in a more flexible graph-like structure,
where records can have multiple connections to
other records, forming complex relationships like
multiple parent-child relationships. This approach
allows for multiple relationships between records,
enabling a richer and more versatile
representation of data.
3. relational databases-Relational databases
represent data using tables consisting of rows
and columns, and relationships between entities
are established through keys (primary and
foreign keys). While relational databases can
represent relationships between entities,
including one-to-many relationships, they do not
inherently enforce a parent-child relationship
structure like hierarchical databases.
So option A is the correct answer.

response time
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
1. Shortest remaining time first (SRTF) scheduling
may cause starvation:
This statement is true. SRTF scheduling prioritizes
the process with the shortest remaining
execution time, which can lead to longer
processes being repeatedly preempted by
shorter ones. If there are always shorter
processes arriving, longer processes may never
get a chance to execute, leading to starvation.
2. Preemptive scheduling may cause starvation:
This statement is true. Preemptive scheduling
allows the operating system to interrupt the
execution of a process to give access to the CPU
to another process. If there are processes with
higher priority constantly arriving, lower priority
processes may be repeatedly preempted and
may never get a chance to execute, resulting in
starvation.
3. Round robin is better than FCFS in terms of
response time:
This statement is true. Round-robin scheduling
ensures fairness by providing each process with a
fixed time slice to execute before being
preempted, which helps in achieving better
response time compared to first-come, first-
served (FCFS) scheduling, especially when there
are long-running processes.
So option D is the correct answer.

question:
In the design protocol of the critical section
problem, each process must ask permission to
enter the critical section in _______ code; it then
executes in the critical section; once it finishes
executing in the critical section it enters the
_____ code. The process then enters the _____
code.

options.B: entry section, exit section, remainder section
options.C: remainder section, entry section, exit section
options.D: remainder section, exit section, entry section

solution:
Entry Section (Entry Code):
In this section, a process must request permission
or acquire a lock to enter the critical section.
Before entering the critical section, the process
must ensure that it has exclusive access to the
shared resource by using synchronization
mechanisms such as locks, semaphores, or
mutexes. If the resource is currently being used
by another process, the process requesting
access to the critical section may need to wait or
be placed in a queue until it can acquire the
necessary lock.
Critical Section:
This is the section of code where the process
performs its critical operations or accesses the
shared resource. It is essential that only one
process executes this section at any given time to
prevent race conditions, data corruption, or
inconsistencies.
Exit Section (Exit Code):
After completing its operations in the critical
section, the process releases the lock or
permission it acquired in the entry section,
allowing other processes to enter the critical
section if they are waiting. Releasing the lock
ensures that other processes can access the
shared resource once the current process has
finished using it.
Remainder Section (Remainder Code):
This section contains the remainder of the
process's code that is not part of the critical
section. It includes any non-critical operations or

question:
How do you create agile processes to manage
unpredictability?
1.Requirements gathering must be conducted
very carefully.
2.Risk analysis must be conducted before
planning takes place.
3.Software increments must be delivered in short
time periods.
4.Software processes must not adapt to changes
incrementally.

given below:
solution:
1. Requirements gathering must be conducted
very carefully:
While requirements gathering is important in any
software development process, including agile,
being overly meticulous can lead to rigid plans
that are difficult to adjust when unpredictability
occurs. Agile processes encourage iterative and
collaborative requirement gathering, where
requirements are refined and adjusted as the
project progresses based on feedback and
changing priorities.
2. Risk analysis must be conducted before
planning takes place:

mitigation strategies and incorporate flexibility
so agile methodology performs risk analysis
throughout the process not only at the
beginning.

short time periods.

working software in short, iterative cycles known
as iterations. By breaking down the project into
smaller increments, teams can quickly adapt to
changing requirements, receive feedback from
stakeholders, and adjust priorities based on
emerging insights, thereby managing
unpredictability more effectively.
4. Software processes must not adapt to changes
incrementally:
 Agile processes advocate for incremental and
iterative adaptation to changes throughout the
project lifecycle. By embracing change and
adjusting processes incrementally, teams can
respond more effectively to unpredictable
events, evolving requirements, and shifting
priorities.

question:
Circuit satisfiability problem: Given a Boolean
combinatorial circuit composed of AND, OR, and
NOT gates, is it satisfiable? A one-output
Boolean combinatorial circuit is satisfiable means
for the given inputs the output will be 1.
1. The circuit satisfiability problem belongs to
class NP
2. The circuit satisfiability problem is at least as
hard as any language in NP
3. The circuit satisfiability is NP-Complete
4. The size of the circuit is (K+1)
5. If PNP, this situation would contradict the
NP-Completeness of the problem.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
1. The circuit satisfiability problem belongs to
class NP: This statement is true. The circuit
satisfiability problem can be verified in
polynomial time. Given a set of inputs that satisfy
the circuit (i.e., make the output 1), we can verify
whether the output is 1 by simply traversing the
circuit once. If the output is 1, then the inputs
satisfy the circuit, and this verification process
can be done in polynomial time.
2. The circuit satisfiability problem is at least as
hard as any language in NP: This statement is
true and reflects the fact that the circuit
satisfiability problem is NP-hard. Any problem in
NP can be reduced to the circuit satisfiability
problem in polynomial time. This means that if we
had a polynomial-time algorithm for solving the
circuit satisfiability problem, we could use it to
solve any problem in NP in polynomial time,
making P = NP.
3. The circuit satisfiability is NP-Complete: This
statement is also true. The circuit satisfiability
problem is both in NP (as explained in statement
1) and NP-hard (as explained in statement 2).
Therefore, it is NP-complete, meaning it is one of
the hardest problems in NP.
4. The size of the circuit is (K+1): Suppose A is a
decision problem that is solvable in p(n) time by
some program P, where n is the length of the
input. Also, assume that the input is represented
as a sequence of bits. Then, for every fixed n,
there is a circuit Cn of size about O((p(n)) · (log
p(n))O(1))
such that for every input x = (x1, . . . , xn) of length
n, we have
A(x) = Cn(x1, . . . , xn)
That is, circuit Cn solves problem A on all the
inputs of length n.
5. If P ≠ NP, it wouldn't contradict the existence of
NP-complete problems. In fact, NP-completeness
arises precisely because we believe that P and
NP are different.
When:
P ≠ NP: This conjecture implies that there exist
problems in NP that are not in P, meaning they
cannot be solved in polynomial time. These are
problems for which there's no known algorithm
that can solve them efficiently (in polynomial
time) but for which a solution can be verified
efficiently (in polynomial time).
NP-Completeness: A problem is NP-complete if it
is in NP and every problem in NP can be reduced
to it in polynomial time. In other words, an NP-
complete problem is at least as hard as the
hardest problems in NP.
So option C is the correct answer.

The Solution to Silly Window Syndrome problem
is/are:
I. Nagle's Algorithm
II. Clark's Algorithm
III. Jacobson's Algorithm
IV. Piggy backing Algorithm
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Silly Window Syndrome is a problem that arises
due to poor implementation of TCP. It degrades
the TCP performance and makes the data
transmission extremely inefficient. The problem is
called so because: 
 It causes the sender window size to shrink to
a silly value. 
 The window size shrinks to such an extent
that the data being transmitted is smaller than
TCP Header. 
The two major causes of this syndrome are as
follows: 
The sender window transmits one byte of data
repeatedly. 
The receiver window accepts one byte of data
repeatedly. 
 Cause-1: Sender window transmitting one
byte of data repeatedly – 
Suppose only one byte of data is generated
by an application. The poor implementation of
TCP leads to the transmission of this small
segment of data. Every time the application
generates a byte of data, the window
transmits it. This makes the transmission
process slow and inefficient. The problem is
solved by Nagle’s algorithm. 
Nagle’s algorithm suggests:
The sender should send only the first byte on
receiving one-byte data from the application. 
The sender should buffer all the rest bytes
until the outstanding byte gets
acknowledged. 
The sender should wait for 1 RTT(Round Trip
Time). 
 After receiving the acknowledgment, the
sender should send the buffered data in one
TCP segment. Then, the sender should buffer
the data again until the previously sent data
gets acknowledged. 
Cause-2: Receiver window accepting one byte
of data repeatedly – 
Suppose consider the case when the receiver
is unable to process all the incoming data. In
such a case, the receiver will advertise a small
window size. The process continues and the
window size becomes smaller and smaller. A
stage arrives when it repeatedly advertises a
window size of 1 byte. This makes the
receiving process slow and inefficient. The
solution to this problem is Clark’s Solution. 
Clark’s solution suggests: 
The receiver should not send a window
update for 1 byte. 
The receiver should wait until it has a decent
amount of space available. 
The receiver should then advertise that
window size to the sender. 
So option A is the correct answer.
Jacobson’s algorithm is used for congestion
control by giving dynamic TOT (time-out timer).
Piggy backing Algorithm - Piggybacking is the
technique of delaying outgoing acknowledgment
and attaching it to the next data packet. This is
used to improve the efficiency of Network.

separable, much like the AND operation. It is

separable, just like the OR operation. To put it
simply, the NOR operation is the opposite of the

question:
Choose the correct option describing the
features of Artificial neural network
I. It is essentially machine learning algorithm.
II. It is useful when solving the problems for
which the data set is very large.
III. They are able to extract features without input
from the programmer.
Iv. These are systems modeled on the human
brain and nervous system

given below:

options.D: All the statements are not correct.

solution:
I. It is essentially machine learning algorithm.
Explanation: This statement is true. An Artificial
Neural Network (ANN) is a machine-learning
model inspired by the human brain's neural
structure. It comprises interconnected nodes
(neurons) organized into layers. Data flows
through these nodes, adjusting the weights of
connections to learn patterns and make
predictions.
II. It is useful when solving problems for which
the data set is very large.
Explanation: This statement is true. Neural
networks can provide robust solutions to
problems in a wide range of disciplines,
particularly areas involving classification,
prediction, filtering, optimization, pattern
recognition, and function approximation where
the data set is very large.
III. They are able to extract features without input
from the programmer.
Explanation: This statement is true. One of its key
advantages is the capacity to automatically find
the representations required for feature
detection or classification from raw data so they
are able to automatically extract features without
feeding the input by the programmer.
IV. These are systems modeled on the human
brain and nervous system
Explanation: This statement is true. The
structures and operations of human neurons
serve as the basis for artificial neural networks. It
is also known as neural networks or neural nets.
The input layer of an artificial neural network is
the first layer, and it receives input from external
sources and releases it to the hidden layer, which
is the second layer. In the hidden layer, each
neuron receives input from the previous layer
neurons, computes the weighted sum, and sends
it to the neurons in the next layer. These
connections are weighted means effects of the
inputs from the previous layer are optimized
more or less by assigning different-different
weights to each input and it is adjusted during
the training process by optimizing these weights
for improved model performance. 
So option A is the correct answer.

question:
An OS follows round-robin scheduling with time
quantum of 4 ms. Assuming that the CPU is free
now and there are 20 processes waiting in the
ready queue, the maximum amount of time that
a process waits before getting into the CPU is
_____.
solution:
- In round-robin scheduling, every process gets
an equal share of CPU time, which is defined by
the time quantum or time slice. Assuming there's
no context switching time, each process will get
to use the CPU for the duration of the time
quantum then get placed at the end of the ready
queue.
- In this case, the time quantum is 4 m s and there
are 2 0 processes in total.

once equals to "number of processes" times
"time quantum", this means one cycle will take
20* 4=80 ms.
- Given that the CPU is free now, the first process
doesn't have to wait, so it gets the CPU
immediately. But the last process, i.e., the 20th
process has to wait for 19 processes (not the full
20, because the first process didn't wait) to
complete their quanta before getting CPU. That
means
- Maximum wait time =( Number of processes -1) *
Time quantum
- Maximum waiting time for a process is 19 * 4=76
ms.

question:
What is the probability that a positive integer
selected at random from the set of positive
integers not exceeding 100 is divisible by either
2 or 5?
solution:
Let E1 be the event that the integer is divisible by
2 and E2 be the event that it is divisible 5. Then
the event that the integer is divisible by 2 or 5 is
E1 ∪  E2 and E1 ∩  E2 is the event that it is divisible
by 2 and 5. It follows that:
p(E1 ∪  E2) = p(E1) + p(E2) − p(E1 ∩  E2) ---------- (1)
Here, a positive integer not exceeding 100, so
the total number of outcomes will be 100
From 1 to 100, there are a total of 50 numbers
that are divisible by 2, so favorable number of
outcomes E1 = 50
From 1 to 100, there are a total of 20 numbers
that are divisible by 5, so favorable number of
outcomes E2 = 20
From 1 to 100, there are a total of 10 numbers
that are divisible by 2 and 5, so favorable number
of outcomes E1 ∩  E2 = 10
So from equation (1)
p(E1 ∪  E2)= 50/100 + 20/100 − 10/100 = 3/5.
Therefore option B is the correct answer.

question: Which of the following is TRUE?

options.A:
The cost of searching an AVL tree is (log n)
but that of binary search is O(n)
options.B:
The cost of searching an AVL tree in (log n)
but that of complete binary tree is (n log n)
options.C:
The cost of searching a binary tree is 0(log n)
but that of AVL tree is (n)
options.D:
The cost of searching an AVL tree is (n log n)
but that of a binary search tree is O(n)

solution:
AVL trees and binary search trees are two
commonly used data structures for storing and
searching data. Both these data structures are
binary trees, which means that each node can
have at most two child nodes. However, AVL
trees are self-balancing binary search trees, while
binary search trees may or may not be balanced.
Searching in AVL Trees and Binary Search Trees:
Searching for a value in a binary search tree or an
AVL tree involves traversing the tree from the
root node to a leaf node that contains the value.
The cost of searching a tree is determined by the
number of nodes that must be visited to find the
value. In a balanced tree, the cost of searching is
proportional to the height of the tree.
The Cost of Searching AVL Trees and Binary
Search Trees: The cost of searching an AVL tree is
logarithmic, which means that the number of
nodes that must be visited to find a value is
proportional to the logarithm of the number of
nodes in the tree. The cost of searching a binary
search tree is also logarithmic if the tree is
balanced. However, if the binary search tree is
unbalanced, the cost of searching may be linear,
which means that the number of nodes that must
be visited may be proportional to the number of
nodes in the tree. 
The cost of searching an AVL tree is (log n) but
that of a binary search tree is O(n) if the binary
search tree is unbalanced. However, if the binary
search tree is balanced, the cost of searching is
also (log n). AVL trees are always balanced, so
the cost of searching is guaranteed to be
logarithmic. Therefore, the correct answer is
option 'A'.

Gray code is a binary numbering system in which
two successive values only differ by one bit is
called gray code.
The prefix and reflect method are recursively
used to generate the Gray code of a number. For
generating gray code:
1. We find the number of bits required to
represent a number.
2. Next, we find the code for 0, i.e., 0000, which
is the same as binary.
3. Now, we take the previous code, i.e., 0000,
and change the most significant bit of it.
4. We perform this process reclusively until all the
codes are uniquely identified.
5. If by changing the most significant bit, we find
the same code obtained previously, then the
second most significant bit will be changed, and
so on.
 So the correct answer is C.
BCD is a binary-encoded representation of
decimal numbers. In this, each decimal digit is
represented by a group of 4 binary digits or bits
in much the same way as Hexadecimal. So for the
10 decimal digits (0-to-9), we need a 4-bit binary
code. 
The excess-3 code is a BCD code used to
represent the decimal numbers. 
We can find the excess-3 code of the given
binary number by using the following steps:
We find the decimal number of the given binary
number.
Then we add 3 in each digit of the decimal
number.
Now, we find the binary code of each digit of the
newly generated decimal number.
We can also add 0011 in each 4-bit BCD code of
the decimal number for getting an excess-3
code.

Logical Shift 
The number of bit positions in a given value shall
be shifted, such as a shift left by 1, and the empty
position in the least significant bit is filled with 0.
A logical shift does not preserve a number's sign
bit. 
Circular shift
A rotation (or circular shift) is an operation in
which the bits that fall off at one end are put
back to the other end. This maintains the number
of bits in data does not divide the number.
Arithmetic shift left
A left arithmetic shift of a binary number by 1.
The empty position in the least significant bit is
filled with a zero which multiplies the number by
2.
So option C is the correct answer.

Consider a triangle PQR with coordinates as
P(0,0), Q(2,2) and R(10,4). If this triangle is to be
magnified to four times its size while keeping
R(10,4) fixed, then the coordinates of the
magnified triangle are :

To magnify a shape, we can use the principle of
scalings in transformations. We keep the points

factor of 4 from that point.

 Start with the point P(0,0)

factor) to get (-40,-16).

the new position for P, R+4x(P-R)=(10,4)+

Similarly, for point Q(2,2).

The coordinates of the magnified triangle are

options.C:

solution:
A function that is declared in a base class but not
implemented there is known as a pure virtual
function. Rather, it needs to be implemented in
any derived class that isn't abstract.
A pure virtual function often has the following
syntax:
virtual void print() = 0 ;
Option A) Virtual functions do not implement
polymorphism:
This statement is false. Virtual functions are a
fundamental feature of polymorphism in object-
oriented programming. Polymorphism allows
objects of different types to be treated as
objects of a common base type, and virtual
functions enable dynamic method binding, which
is essential for achieving polymorphic behavior.
Option (B) Virtual functions do not permit calling
of derived class functions using a base class
pointer:
This statement is false. Virtual functions allow
derived class functions to be invoked through a
base class pointer or reference. 
Option C) We can never build an object from a
class containing a pure virtual function
Classes classified as abstract have one or more
pure virtual functions. The aim of an abstract
class is to provide a suitable base class from
which other classes can inherit. Abstract classes
can be seen as an interface and cannot be
utilized to instantiate objects. A compilation error
occurs when you try to instantiate an object of
an abstract class.
Option D) Pure virtual function can never have a
body
This statement is false. Pure virtual functions can
have a body, but it's optional. When a pure virtual
function has a body, it provides a default
implementation that can be overridden by
derived classes. 
So option C is the correct answer.

question: An Address in main memory is called:
solution:
A memory address is a reference to a specific
memory location used at various levels by
software and hardware.
An address that is created by the CPU while a
program is running is known as a logical
address. Because the logical address is virtual
that is, it doesn't exist physically—it is also
referred to as a virtual address. The CPU uses
this address as a reference to go to the
physical memory location. 
A physical address is the actual address in the
main memory where data is stored. It is a
location in physical memory, as opposed to a
virtual address. Physical addresses are used by
the Memory Management Unit (MMU) to
translate logical addresses into physical
addresses.
The fundamental difference between logical
and physical addresses is that the CPU
generates the logical address during program
execution, on the other hand, the physical
address refers to a location in the memory
unit.

question:
The head of a moving head disk with 200 tracks,
numbered 0 to 199, has just finished a request at
track 125, and currently serving a request at track
143. The queue of requests is given in the FIFO
order as 86,147,91,177,94,150,102,175,130. What
will be the total number of head movements
required to satisfy these requests for SCAN
algorithm?
solution:
SCAN Disk Scheduling Algorithm
Step 1 − The array has the elements that have
requested resources from different processes in
ascending order based on arrival time.
Step 2 − The disk arm starts from one end of the
disk and moves towards the other end.
Step 3 − When the disk moves in this direction, it
will service all tracks one by one based on the
request.
Step 4 − Then calculate the total distance
traveled from the head.
Step 5 − The new position is identified by the
currently serviced request
Step 6 − Then step 3 is repeated when it reaches
one end of the disk.
Step 7 − When the endpoint is reached, it will
reverse the direction and go back to step 2 when
the entire request has been serviced.
In the given question, the head has just finished a
request at track 125 and is currently at track 143.
That means it is moving towards a higher number
of tracks.
So we will take the difference between the
highest track number and the current track
number. i.e. 199-143=56.
Then for the reverse direction we will take the
difference between the highest track number
and smallest track number i.e. 199-86=113
Then we will add both the differences i.e. 56+113
=169 cylinders

question:
Which collision resolution technique involves
maintaining a linked list of collided keys?
solution:
Option A, With linear probing, every hash table
cell is viewed as a slot with the capacity to hold a
single key-value pair. This is an open-addressing
technique.
The algorithm looks through the table linearly
until it finds an empty slot when a collision
happens. One drawback of linear probing is that
it may result in clustering, which is the filling of a
group of nearby cells, hence lengthening the
average search time.
Option B, Quadratic probing is an open
addressing method designed to handle collisions,
much like linear probing. But upon collision,
rather than looking for an empty slot linearly.
Quadratic probing uses a quadratic function
h(value)=(h(value)+i)% size, where i is the
attempt number.
Option C, The process of implementing each cell
in the Hach table as a distinct linked list or any
other dynamic data structure is known as
chaining.
In the event of a collision, the key-value pair is
kept in the same slot as the linked list's
subsequent node. This eliminates the need for a
space in the hash table to manage collisions and
offers a simple and effective method of doing so.
The drawback, though, is the possibility of
inefficiency brought on by a mishandled key
distribution or collided keys. It can cause some
chains to get extremely long while others get
short or empty.
Option D, Double hashing, a collision resolution
technique in hash tables, that uses two hash
functions to compute two different hash values
for a key. This method is less susceptible to
clustering than linear probing and quadratic
probing but more computation is required to
calculate two hash functions.
So option C is the correct answer.
