question:
If N=NxN, N is set of natural numbers and R is
relation on N, s.t. RCN X Ni.e. <x,y> R <u,v>
xv=yu, then which of the following are TRUE?
(A) Reflexive
(B) Symmetric
(C) Transitive
(D) Asymmetric
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
(A)
solution:
The properties of the relation R are defined as
<x,y> R <u,v> xv=yu
(A) Reflexive:
For a relation to be reflexive, (a, a) must be in the
relation for every element a in the set. In this
case, we have x=u and y=v. So,(u, u) and (v, v)
must be in the relation.
Since N is the set of natural numbers, for any
natural number u or v, (u, u) and (v,v) are in the
relation. Therefore, the relation is reflexive.
(B) Symmetric:
For a relation to be symmetric, if (a,b) is in the
relation, then (b, a) must also be in the relation
for every pair (a, b). In this case, (x, y) is in the
relation if and only if(y, x) is in the relation as
xv=yu implies yu=xv. Therefore, the relation is
symmetric.
(C) Transitive:
For a relation to be transitive, if (a,b) and (b,c) are
in the relation, then (a, c) must also be in the
relation for every triplet (a, b, c). In this case, if
xv=yu and yw=zv, then multiplying these
equations gives xw=zu, which implies (x,w) is in
the relation. Therefore, the relation is transitive.
(D) Asymmetric:
For a relation to be asymmetric, if (a, b) is in the
relation, then (b, a) must not be in the relation for
any pair (a, b). In this case, since (x, y) is in the
relation if and only if (y, x) is also in the relation,
the relation cannot be asymmetric.
So option D is the correct answer.

question:
The interface(s) that provide(s) I/0 transfer of
data directly to and from the memory unit
peripheral is/are termed as:
(A) DMA (Direct Memory Access)
(B) IOP (Input-Output Processor)
(C) Serial Interface
(D) Parallel Interface
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
(A) (A) Only
(B) (B) Only
(C)
solution:
DMA (Direct Memory Access):
DMA is a feature that allows peripherals to
transfer data directly to and from the memory
without the intervention of the CPU.
Instead of the CPU being involved in each
data transfer between peripherals (like
storage devices, network interfaces, etc) and
memory, DMA enables the peripherals to
communicate directly with the memory.
This improves overall system efficiency by
offloading data transfer tasks from the CPU.
IOP (Input-Output Processor):
An IOP is a processor specifically designed to
handle input and output operations. It serves
as a dedicated unit for managing
communication between peripherals and the
rest of the system, including the memory.
The IOP takes care of coordinating data
transfers, handling interrupts, and managing
other aspects of input and output it helps to
offload these tasks from the main CPU,
allowing it to focus on more complex
computations.
So, both DMA and IOP are interfaces or features
that facilitate the direct transfer of data between
peripherals and the memory unit without
requiring constant involvement of the main CPU.
They contribute to improving the efficiency and
performance of the overall system by
streamlining data transfer operations.
Both serial and parallel interfaces can be used for
data communication in computer systems, they
are typically not used for direct communication
with main memory in modern architectures.
Instead, high-speed serial interfaces like
 Peripheral Component Interconnect (PCI) are
commonly employed for connecting main
memory modules (RAM) directly to the CPU and
other components on the motherboard.
So option C is the correct answer.

Which of the statements are CORRECT?
(A) Constructors are invoked automatically when
the objects are created.
(B) Constructors do not have return types, not
even void, and therefore they cannot return
values.

derived class can call the base class constructors.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :

Which one of the following statements is
CORRECT?
(A) Granularity is the size of data items in a
database.
(B) Two operations in a schedule are said to be in
conflict if they belong to the same transaction.
(C) Two schedulers are said to be conflict
equivalent if the order of any two conflicting
operations is the same in both schedules.
(D) Write operations that are performed without
performing the write operation are known as
Blind Writes.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
(A) (A) and (B) Only
(B)
solution:
Statement A - Granularity is the size of data
items in a database.
It is the maximum size of a data item that can be
locked. Multiple granularity refers to the
hierarchical partitioning of the database into
blocks that are trackable and able to be locked,
depending on what has to be locked and how. A
tree is a graphic representation of such a
hierarchy. 
Take the tree, for instance, which has four levels
of nodes. The database as a whole is represented
at the highest level. It is followed by nodes of
type area; these are the areas that make up the
database. Files are the children nodes in the
area.Finally, each file has child nodes called
records.
All of a node's descendants are implicitly locked
in the same lock mode when a transaction locks a
node, whether in shared or exclusive mode.
Statement B: Two operations in a schedule are
said to be in conflict if they belong to the same
transaction.
Two operations in a schedule are said to conflict
if they access the same item X; and at least one
of the operations is a write_item(X). For example,
in schedule S1, the operations r1(X) and w2(X)
conflict, as do the operations r2(X) and w1(X),
and the operations w1(X) and w2(X). However,
the operations r1(X) and r2(X) do not conflict,
since they are both read operations; the
operations w2(X) and w1(Y) do not conflict
because they operate on distinct data items X
and Y. So Statement B is correct.
Statement C : Two schedulers are said to be
conflict equivalent if the order of any two
conflicting operations is the same in both
schedules.
In a database system, a schedule is a sequence of
operations (such as read and write operations)
performed by transactions in the system. Two
schedules are view-equivalent if they produce
the same set of results when executed against
the same database state.
A schedule S1 is said to be view-equivalent to a
schedule S2 if and only if:
The order of any two conflicting operations in S1
is the same as the order of those operations in
S2. A conflicting operation is an operation that
accesses the same data item as another
operation and at least one of the operations is a
write operation.
So Statement C is correct.
Statement D: Write operations that are
performed without performing the write
operation are known as Blind Writes.
A blind write refers to a write operation on a
database that does not first acquire locks on the
data it is modifying. In a typical database system,
before writing data, exclusive locks would be
acquired to prevent other transactions from
reading or writing the same data at the same
time.
So statement D is incorrect. 
Therefore option B is the correct answer.

question:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT
?
(A) A process always check state of currently
executing process to enter critical schema.
(B) Spin locks use busy waiting.
(C) Periodically testing a variable until some
value appears is known as busy waiting.
(D) Critical region is a part of the program, where
shared memory is kept.
(E) Printer daemon, continuously checks to see if
there are any file to be printed.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
(A)
solution:
Statement A: A process always check state of
currently executing process to enter critical
schema.
A process does not always need to check the
state of the currently executing process to enter
the critical section. It just needs to ensure mutual
exclusion i.e. if another process is executing in its
critical section, then no other process can enter
the critical section. So statement A is incorrect.
Statement B: Spinlocks use busy waiting. 
Spinlock is a synchronization mechanism where
multiple processes access shared resources
without interfering with each other. It is used in
operating systems to protect shared resources
from single access by multiple threads or
processes. Spinlocks use a busy-wait method,
where a thread continuously selects a lock until it
becomes available. So statement B is correct.
Statement C: Critical region is a part of the
program, where shared memory is kept.
A concurrent program's crucial region, sometimes
referred to as its critical section, is the area where
access to shared resources needs to be tightly
controlled. This is required to ensure that errors
or inconsistent program output are not caused
by concurrent access to shared resources. So
statement C is correct.
Statement D: Printer daemon, continuously
checks to see if there are any file to be printed.
Printer and other output devices often respond
to interrupts or other signals generated when a
new print job arrives. This depends on the
implementation of the software. So statement D
is incorrect.
Therefore option C is the correct answer.

question:
Three address codes can be represented in

(B) Triples
(C) Patterns
(D) Indirect Triples
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
(A) (A) and (B) Only
(B)

Three address code is a intermediate code which
can be easily converted to machine code. It uses
at most three addresses and one operator to
represent an expression and the value computed
at each instruction is stored in temporary
variable generated by compiler. The compiler
decides the order of operation given by three
address code. 
Option A,  Quadruple – It is a structure that
consists of 4 fields namely op, arg1, arg2 and
result. op denotes the operator and arg1 and
arg2 denotes the two operands and the result is
used to store the result of the expression.

make use of an extra temporary variable to

reference to another triple’s value is needed, a
pointer to that triple is used. So, it consists of

a set of rules that a scanner follows to create a
token. Tokens are a sequence of characters
represented as a unit that cannot be further
broken down.

makes use of a pointer to the listing of all
references to computations which is made
separately and stored. It's similar in utility as
compared to quadruple representation but

implicit and easier to rearrange code.

question:
The selection of Spiral Model based on
characteristics of requirements :
(A) Are requirements easily understandable and

cycle?

built

solution:

risk-driven model that involves four phases:
planning, risk analysis, engineering, and
evaluation. This model is ideal for large, complex,
and innovative projects when frequent releases
are necessary.

stakeholder faith in the final product.

question:
Which of the following statement/s is/are NOT
CORRECT?
(A) OSPF is based on distance-vector routing
protocol.
(B) Both link-state and distance-vector routing
are based on the least cost goal.
(C) BGP4 is based on the path-vector algorithm.
(D) The three-node instability can be avoided
using split horizon combined with poison reverse.
(E) RIP is based on link state algorithm.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
(A) (A), (D) and (E) Only
(B)
solution:
(A) OSPF is based on distance-vector routing
protocol.- This statement is FALSE.
Explanation: Using its own shortest path first
(SPF) algorithm, open shortest path first (OSPF) is
a link-state routing protocol that determines the
optimal path between the source and the
destination router. In contrast to distance-vector
routing protocols, which interchange the routing
table over time, link-state routing protocols rely
solely on the concept of triggered updates—that
is, updates are only sent in response to changes
noticed in the learned routing table. 
(B) Both link-state and distance-vector routing
are based on the least cost goal- This statement
is TRUE.
Distance Vector Routing – 
It is a dynamic routing algorithm in which each
router computes a distance between itself and
each possible destination i.e. its immediate
neighbors.
The router shares its knowledge about the whole
network with its neighbors and accordingly
updates the table based on its neighbors.
The sharing of information with the neighbors
takes place at regular intervals.
Link State Routing – 
It is a dynamic routing algorithm in which each
router shares knowledge of its neighbors with
every other router in the network.
A router sends its information about its
neighbors only to all the routers through
flooding.
Information sharing takes place only whenever
there is a change.
(C) BGP4 is based on the path-vector algorithm -
This statement is TRUE.
A path-vector routing protocol is a network
routing protocol that maintains the path
information that gets updated dynamically.
Updates that have looped through the network
and returned to the same node are easily
detected and discarded.  Border Gateway
Protocol (BGP) is a standardized exterior
gateway protocol designed to exchange routing
and reachability information among autonomous
systems (AS) on the Internet. BGP is classified as
a path-vector routing protocol, and it makes
routing decisions based on paths, network
policies, or rule sets configured by a network
administrator.
(D) The three-node instability can be avoided
using a split-horizon combined with poison
reverse.- This statement is FALSE
Counting to infinity is a drawback of distance-
vector routing. While cost increases (bad news)
propagate slowly, cost decreases (positive news)
propagate quickly. Distance-vector routing takes
some time for all other routers to become aware
of a broken connection (cost becomes infinity),
      |       |   


UGC	NET
which is necessary for a routing protocol to
function properly. 
Split-horizon route advertisement is a method
of preventing routing loops in distance-vector
routing protocols by prohibiting a router from
advertising a route back onto the interface
from which it was learned.
With poison reverse, route advertisements
that would be suppressed by split horizon are
instead advertised with a distance of infinity.
With the help of split horizon and poison reverse,
the two-node instability can be prevented.
However, stability cannot be assured if instability
occurs between three nodes. The instability
between three nodes is referred to as three-node
instability
(E) RIP is based on the link state algorithm - This
statement is FALSE.
Routing Information Protocol (RIP) is a dynamic
routing protocol that uses hop count as a routing
metric to find the best path between the source
and the destination network.
So option A is the correct answer.

question:

voltage defined bit is 0 (zero).

rate of N / 2.

(B)
solution:
(A) NRZ is a bipolar scheme in which the
positive voltage defined bit is 0 (zero).- This
statement is FALSE.
Explanation: A non-return-to-zero (NRZ) line
code is a binary code in which ones are
represented by one significant condition, usually
a positive voltage, while zeros are represented by
some other significant condition, usually a
negative voltage, with no other neutral or rest
condition.
(B) NRZ-L and NRZ-I both have an average
signal rate of N / 2.- This statement is TRUE.
Explanation: NRZ-L ( Nonreturn to Zero-Level) is
the code used to generate or interpret digital
data by terminals and other devices. If a different
code is to be used for transmission, it is
generated from an NRZ-L signal by the
transmission system.
As with NRZ-L, NRZI maintains a constant voltage
pulse for the duration of a bit of time. The data
themselves are encoded as the presence or
absence of a signal transition at the beginning of
the bit time. A transition (low to high or high to
low) at the beginning of a bit time denotes a
binary 1 for that bit time; no transition indicates a
binary 0. In both signal drops (but does not
return to zero) in the middle of the bit period.
The average signal rate in both cases is N / 2. 
(C) The idea of RZ and NRZ-L are combined into
the Manchester scheme. - This statement is
TRUE.
Explanation: Manchester encoding is a
synchronous clock encoding technique used by
the physical layer of the Open System
Interconnection [OSI] to encode the clock and
data of a synchronous bit stream. Differential
Manchester, combines the idea of RZ and NRZ-I.
There is always a transition in the middle of the
bit, but the bit values are determined at the
beginning of the bit. if the next bit is zero there is
a transition if the next bit is 1 there is none. 
(D) NRZ-L and NRZ-I both have DC component
problems.- This statement is TRUE
Explanation: When the voltage level remains
constant for long periods of time, there is an
increase in the low frequencies of the signal.
Most channels are band pass and may not
support the low frequencies. This is known as DC
problem. both NRZ-L and NRZ-I maintain a
constant voltage level for the entire bit period.
So both have DC component problems. 
(E) The minimum bandwidth of Manchester and
differential Manchester is 3 times that of NRZ. -
This statement is FALSE.
Explanation: The Manchester and differential
Manchester Encoding consumes twice the
bandwidth of the original signal not 3 times.
So option C is the correct answer.

bd. If the Goal is not found at this point, DFS
unwinds (the stack is popped), perhaps all the

space used. So the Worst case space complexity

question:
In most general case, the computer needs to
process each instruction with the following
sequence of steps:
(A) Calculate the effective address
(B) Execute the instruction
(C) Fetch the instruction from memory
(D) Fetch the operand from memory
(E) Decode the instruction

given below :

solution:
Explanation:
In computer organization, an instruction cycle,
also known as a fetch-decode-execute cycle, is
the basic operation performed by a central
processing unit (CPU) to execute an instruction.
The instruction cycle consists of several steps,
each of which performs a specific function in the
execution of the instruction.
Fetch: In the fetch cycle, the CPU retrieves the
instruction from memory. The instruction is
typically stored at the address specified by the
program counter (PC). The PC is then
incremented to point to the next instruction in
memory.
Decode: In the decode cycle, the CPU interprets
the instruction and determines what operation
needs to be performed. This involves identifying
the opcode and any operands that are needed to
execute the instruction.
Calculate the effective address. If the
instruction has an operand, it's not usually the
actual data but rather its address that is
specified. During this phase, the address for the
operands is computed. The calculated effective
address will be used to fetch the operand in the
next step.
Fetch operands: In some CPUs, the operands
needed for an instruction are fetched during a
separate cycle before the execute cycle. This is
called the fetch operands cycle.
Execute: In the execute cycle, the CPU performs
the operation specified by the instruction. This
may involve reading or writing data from or to
memory, performing arithmetic or logic
operations on data, or manipulating the control
flow of the program.

question:
Arrange the following levels of interrupt
protection within the Linux Kernel, in the order of
increasing priority.
(a) user mode programs
(b) bottom half interrupt handlers
(c) kernel system service routines
(d) top half interrupt handlers
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
solution:
Interrupt: An interrupt is an event that alters the
sequence of instructions executed by a
processor in corresponding to the electrical
signal generated by the HW circuit both inside &
outside the CPU.
Following are the uses and priority of the
interrupts in Linux kernel-
(a) user mode programs- These are applications
that are currently running on our computer. They
have the lowest degree of system privileges and
don't communicate directly with other programs
or the system hardware. They ask the kernel for
system services and resources.
(b) kernel system service routines- These
procedures provide system services, which help
the user mode programs. Since they deal directly
with hardware and system structures, they
function at a higher privilege level than user
programs, but they are not as prioritized as
interrupt handlers.
(c) bottom half interrupt handlers -  The Job of
the Bottom half is used to run leftover (deferred)
work by the top halves. When this piece of code
is being executed interrupt is Enabled and
Scheduler is Disabled. The bottom half then
performs whatever other work is required, such
as awakening processes, starting up another I/O
operation, and so on. This setup permits the top
half to service a new interrupt while the bottom
half is still working. Every serious interrupt
handler is split this way.
(d) top half interrupt handlers- Top halves
execute as soon as the CPU receives the
interrupt. In the Top Halves, Context Interrupt
and Scheduler are disabled. This part of the code
only contains Critical Code. The execution time of
this code should be as short as possible because
at this time Interrupt is disabled. When a top-half
handler is called, it will handle the hardware
operations and then add the bottom-half
handler(s) to the interrupt queue because it is
the highest priority.
So the correct answer is option B.

is lexical analysis, also known as scanning. This

question:
Arrange the following encoding strategies used
in Genetic Algorithms (GAs) in the correct
sequence starting from the initial step and
ending with the final representation of solutions :
(a) Binary Encoding
(b) Real valued Encoding
(c) Permutation Encoding
(d) Gray coding
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
solution:
In Genetic algorithms, a chromosome (also
sometimes called a genotype) is a set of
parameters that define a proposed solution to
the problem that the evolutionary algorithm is
trying to solve.
Encoding determines the possible values for
each gene ( It is one element position in the
chromosome.) in a chromosome. Selecting the
correct encoding is one of the challenges in
GA and it is one of the most common
mistakes.
In permutation encoding, every chromosome is
a string of numbers that represent a position in a
sequence. Permutation encoding is useful for
ordering problems.
Example of Problem: Travelling salesman
problem (TSP) 
The problem: There are cities and given distances
between them. The traveling salesman has to
visit all of them, but he does not want to travel
more than necessary. Find a sequence of cities
with a minimal traveled distance.
Encoding: Chromosome describes the order of
cities, in which the salesman will visit them.
Gray coding is a binary numeral system where
two successive values differ in only one bit. In the
context of genetic algorithms. Gray code takes a
binary sequence and shuffles it to form new
sequences.
In binary encoding, every chromosome is a
string of bits - 0 or 1. Binary encoding represents
      |       |   


UGC	NET
a gene in terms of 0 or 1, so a chromosome is
represented by a string of binary bits. 
Example of Problem: Knapsack problem
The problem: There are things with a given value
and size. The knapsack has given capacity. Select
things to maximize the value of things in the
knapsack, but do not extend the knapsack
capacity.
Encoding: Each bit says, whether the
corresponding thing is in knapsack. i.e. 0 =
exclude the item, and 1 = include the item. We
can then sum the included items' values to find
how well that chromosome performs.
Real-value encoding represents a gene with
numeric values, strings, or symbols. The solution
is expressed in its natural state. This encoding is
used when potential solutions contain
continuous values that cannot be encoded easily
with binary encoding.
Example of Problem: Finding weights for a neural
network
The problem: A neural network is given with a
defined architecture. Find weights between
neurons in the neural network to get the desired
output from the network.
Encoding: Real values in chromosomes represent
weights in the neural network.
So encoding schemes where fitness depends
on order only - Permutation
encoding schemes where fitness depends on
value and  order - Binary
encoding schemes where fitness depends on
value only - Real value 
We start with ordering i.e. permutation encoding.
Then we will try to shuffle to form new
sequences using Gray coding. From Gray coding
we will get binary encoding, then we will use
real-value encoding because real-value encoding
is used when potential solutions contain
continuous values that cannot be encoded easily
with binary encoding.
So option C is the correct answer.

question:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I): A thread is a dispatchable unit of
work that does not executes sequentially and is
not interruptible
Statement (II): It is not possible to alter the
behaviour of a thread by altering its context
when thread is suspended
In the light of the above statements, choose the
most appropriate answer from the options given
below :

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B:
Both Statement I and Statement II are
incorrect
options.C:
Statement I is correct but Statement II is
incorrect
options.D:
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is
correct

solution:
Statement (I): A thread is a dispatchable unit of
work that does not execute sequentially and is
not interruptible is false because a process, a
thread refers to a single sequential activity being
executed. these activities are also known as
thread of execution or thread control.
Threads run in parallel improving the application
performance. Each such thread has its own CPU
state and stack, but they share the address space
of the process and the environment. Priority can
be assigned to the threads just like the process,
and the highest priority thread is scheduled first.
Each thread has its own Thread Control Block
(TCB). Like the process, a context switch occurs
for the thread, and register contents are saved in
(TCB). As threads share the same address space
and resources, synchronization is also required
for the various activities of the thread. So these
are also interruptible.
Statement (II): It is not possible to alter the
behaviour of a thread by altering its context
when the thread is suspended -Threads also
have states like ready, executing, blocked, etc. A
thread's register values, program counter, and
other execution-related data make up its context.
The context of a suspended thread can be
preserved, changed, and then restored when the
thread starts up again. This permits modifications
to the thread's behavior.
So option B is the correct answer.

Food X contains 6 units of Vitamin D per gram

solution:
Datagram switching is done at the network layer
of the communication system.
1. In datagram networks, each data packet or
datagram is routed independently from the
source to the destination even if they belong
to the same message. The network treats the
packet as if it exists alone.
2. Since the datagrams are treated as
independent units, no dedicated path is fixed
for data transfer. Each datagram is routed by
the intermediate routers using dynamically
changing routing tables. So two successive
packets from the source may follow
completely separate routes to reach
destination. So there is no need of routers to
hold state information about connections.
So statement I is incorrect.
Virtual – circuit network is a category of packet
switching network, where a virtual path is
established between the source and the
destination systems for data communication to
occur.
Phases of Virtual - Circuit Transmission
There are three phases of transmission by virtual
circuits, set up, data transfer and teardown.
1. Set up Phase − In this phase, a virtual circuit or
a route is established from the source to the
destination through number of switches. The
source and destination use global addresses
using which the switches make routing table
entries.
2. Data Transfer − Once the virtual circuit is set
up, all packets follow the route established
during the set up phase adhering to the
routing tables.
3. Teardown Phase − When data transfer is
complete, the source sends a teardown
request. The destination responds using a
teardown confirmation. The switches flush
their routing table entries, thus relinquishing
the circuit. Each router maintains a separate
entry in the routing table for each virtual
circuit that it is a part of.
So statement II is correct.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding
multiple access techniques \& identify the
CORRECT ones.
A. ALOHA is used for multiple access on a shared
medium
B. TDMA uses WALSH TABLES for time slot
allocation
C. CSMA/CD was invented for wireless networks
D. CDMA codes are sequence of number
generated by orthogonal codes
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Statement A: "ALOHA is used for multiple
access on a shared medium"
Correct: ALOHA is a random access protocol
used for multiple access in a shared medium
(such as satellite and wireless communication).
It allows multiple devices to transmit data over
the same channel.
Statement B: "TDMA uses WALSH TABLES for
time slot allocation"
Incorrect: TDMA (Time Division Multiple Access)
allocates time slots to users, but it does not use
Walsh tables.
Walsh tables are used in CDMA (Code Division
Multiple Access) for orthogonal code generation,
not TDMA.
Statement C: "CSMA/CD was invented for
wireless networks"
Incorrect: CSMA/CD (Carrier Sense Multiple
Access with Collision Detection) was designed
for wired Ethernet networks, not wireless.
Wireless networks use CSMA/CA (Collision
Avoidance) instead of CSMA/CD because
detecting collisions is difficult in a wireless
medium.
Statement D: "CDMA codes are sequence of
numbers generated by orthogonal codes"
Correct: CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access)
uses orthogonal codes, such as Walsh codes, to
separate signals.
These codes allow multiple users to transmit over
the same frequency simultaneously without
interference.
Correct Answer: Option D (A & D only)

options.A:

inadvertently by the called function.
options.B:
Functions are supposed to be independent
and isolated modules. This character is lost, if

function

A function that uses global variables does not

based on
A. Designation
B. Definitions
C. Refutable Assertions
D. Formal Review
E. Requirement Elicitation
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Jackson's Principle : Jackson's Principle is a
concept used in software engineering to address
designation, definitions, and refutable assertions
during software design and development. Here’s
how these elements are relevant:
Designation (A): Refers to assigning clear names
or identifiers to components in the system,
ensuring clarity and traceability.
Definitions (B): Ensures all components, terms,
and relationships are well-defined and
unambiguous.
Refutable Assertions (C): Involves making
assertions that are testable and refutable,
allowing for verification and validation.
Why the Other Options are Incorrect:
D. Formal Review: While important in software
engineering, this is not part of Jackson’s Principle.
E. Requirement Elicitation: This is related to
gathering requirements but not directly linked to
Jackson's Principle.
Thus, the key components of Jackson’s Principle
are Designation, Definitions, and Refutable
Assertions, making Option A the correct answer.

question:
Consider a pipeline unit for fixed - point
multiplication of 8-bit integers. Arrange the
following stages in a correct sequence.
Stage A : Consists of two CSAs and it merges
four numbers from previous stage.
Stage B : is a CPA, which adds up the two
numbers
Stage C : is made upto two level of four CSAs.
Stage D : Generates eight partial products.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The steps involved in the fixed-point
multiplication process for 8-bit integers and the
functions of each stage:
Stage D generates eight partial products. In
multiplication, partial products are formed by
multiplying each bit of one number with all bits
of the other number.
Stage C is made up of two levels of four CSAs
(Carry-Save Adders), which help in adding the
partial products.
Stage A consists of two CSAs and merges four
numbers from the previous stage. This stage
helps reduce the number of partial products into
fewer numbers for addition.
Stage B is a CPA (Carry Propagate Adder),
which adds up the two numbers to finalize the
multiplication result.
Thus, the correct order is D, C, A, B.

question:
What will be the right sequence of the phases of
database design-
A. Physical Design
B. Conceptual Design
C. Logical Design
D. Requirement collection and analysis
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The correct sequence of phases for database
design is as follows:
Requirement Collection and Analysis (D): This is
the first step where the needs and requirements
of the system are gathered, and the objectives of
the database system are defined.
Conceptual Design (B): In this phase, a high-level
model of the database is created, which is
independent of the database management
system (DBMS) and physical aspects. It focuses
on the entities, their relationships, and
constraints.
Logical Design (C): This phase involves
translating the conceptual design into a logical
structure that can be implemented in a specific
DBMS, such as a relational model.
Physical Design (A): This phase focuses on the
physical storage and optimization of the
database, deciding how data will be stored and
accessed in the DBMS.
The correct sequence is D, B, C, A.

referred to as alternate keys.

question:
The network using CSMA/CD has a bandwidth of
20 mbps . If the maximum propagation time is 25
μ s (microsecond), what is the minimum size of
the frame?
solution:
The round-trip propagation time 𝑇 is: 
  𝑇  = 2 × Propagation time
   𝑇 = 2 × 25 μ s = 50 μ s
For CSMA/CD, the frame transmission time must
be greater than or equal to the round-trip
propagation time. Thus:
Frame transmission time ≥ 𝑇 = 50 μ s
The minimum frame size can be calculated by:
Frame size = Bandwidth × Frame transmission
time
Since the bandwidth is 20Mbps = 20×10 bits per
second, and the transmission time is 50 μ s =
50×10  seconds:
Frame size = 20×10 × 50×10
Frame size = 20× 50 = 1000 bits

question:
Which of the following/s is/are FALSE statement?
A. An all key relation is always in BCNF since it
has no FDs.
B. A relation that is not in 4NF due to nontrivial
MVD must be decomposed to convert it into a
set of relations in 4 NF .
C. The decomposition removes the redundancy
by the MVD.
D. 3NF is stronger than BCNF.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
A. This statement is TRUE. In a relation where all
attributes are keys (meaning every attribute is
part of a candidate key), there are no functional
dependencies (FDs) that violate BCNF, so the
relation is trivially in BCNF.
B. This statement is TRUE. If a relation violates
4NF due to nontrivial Multi-Valued
Dependencies (MVDs), it must be decomposed
to eliminate the violation and achieve 4NF.
C. This statement is TRUE. Decomposition based
on MVDs removes redundancy by ensuring that
nontrivial MVDs are eliminated, which typically
reduces data duplication.
D.This statement is FALSE. BCNF is stronger than
3NF. BCNF is a stricter form of normalization
compared to 3NF because every determinant in
BCNF must be a candidate key, while 3NF allows
certain exceptions, such as transitive
dependencies where the non-prime attribute is
dependent on another non-prime attribute.
Hence, the false statement is D only.

question:
The kind of symbols for basic syntactic elements
of first-order logic are
A. Constant
B. Domain
C. Predicate
D. Temporal
E. Function
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The basic syntactic elements of First-Order Logic
(FOL) are:
A. Constant: Represents specific, fixed objects
in the domain.
C. Predicate: Represents relations or
properties of objects.
E. Function: Defines mappings from one
object in the domain to another.
Domain (B) refers to the set of all possible
objects but is not a syntactic element itself—it's
more of a semantic concept.
Temporal (D) is part of temporal logic, which is
an extension of first-order logic and not a basic
syntactic element.

Use III: fseek() sets the position of the file

specifically used for that purpose.

its contents, you can use rewind(file_pointer)
to set the pointer back to the beginning.
Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

question:

information in the data warehouse?
solution:
In a data warehouse, the fact table stores the
primary information, which consists of
measurable business data (e.g., sales, revenue,
quantity sold). It references dimension tables
that provide descriptive context.
Fact Table → Stores numeric values
(measurable data) and foreign keys to
dimension tables.
Dimension Table → Stores descriptive
attributes (e.g., product name, customer
details).
Lookup Table → Used for mapping or
validation.
Primary Table → Not a standard term in data
warehousing.

question:
Which of the following is the correct sequence
with regard to service routine?
A. Save contents of processor registers
B. Turn the interrupt facility on
C. Service the device whose flag is set
D. Check which flag is set
E. Restore contents of processor registers
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
A service routine (or Interrupt Service Routine -
ISR) is executed when an interrupt occurs. The
correct sequence ensures proper handling of the
interrupt while preserving the CPU state.
Step-by-Step Execution of Service Routine:
(A) Save contents of processor registers: Before
handling the interrupt, the CPU registers are
saved to prevent data loss.
(D) Check which flag is set: Identify the
interrupt source by checking the status flags.
(C) Service the device whose flag is set: Execute
the necessary operation to handle the interrupt
(e.g., read input, write output).
(E) Restore contents of processor registers:
Restore previously saved register values to
resume execution correctly.
(B) Turn the interrupt facility on: Re-enable
interrupts to allow new interrupts after the
current one is serviced.
Thus, the correct order is A → D → C → E → B.

solution:
Yacc (Yet Another Compiler Compiler) is a tool
used to generate parsers for context-free
grammars. The parser generated by Yacc is an
LALR (Look-Ahead LR) parser, which is a type of

question:
Which of the following description(s) is/are true:
A. Red Black Tree - Guarantees worst case of
O(log n) time for search, insert \& delete.
B. Trie - Used for efficient prefix - based searches.
C. AVL Tree - self balancing binary search tree
with stricker balance criteria.
D. B- Tree - Allows efficient search, inert, delete
operations in disk based system.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
A. Red-Black Tree : True. A Red-Black Tree is a
balanced binary search tree that ensures the
worst-case time complexity for search, insertion,
and deletion is O(log n) due to its balancing
properties.
B. Trie - True. A Trie is a tree-like structure used
for efficient prefix-based searches. It's
particularly useful in applications like auto-
completion or dictionary lookups.
C. AVL Tree - True. An AVL Tree is a self-
balancing binary search tree, and it has a stricter
balancing criterion than other trees, ensuring
that the heights of the left and right subtrees of
any node differ by at most 1.
D. B-Tree - True. A B-Tree is optimized for storage
systems like disks, where multiple keys are stored
in each node. It ensures efficient search, insert,
and delete operations by minimizing the number
of disk accesses required.

question:
Which of the following are not data manipulation
instructions?
A. Call
B. Loud
C. And
D. Increment
E. Shift
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Call:  Call is a control flow instruction. It's used
to jump to a subroutine or function. It doesn't
directly manipulate data within registers or
memory in the same way as other instructions.
Load (Loud in the option): Load (or a similar
instruction like Move) is a data transfer
instruction. It moves data from one location
(e.g., memory) to another (e.g., a register).
While it moves data, it's primarily a transfer,
not a manipulation.
And: And is a logical instruction. It performs a
bitwise AND operation on data, thus
manipulating the data.
Increment: Increment adds 1 to a value,
directly manipulating the data.
Shift: Shift moves the bits of a value left or
right, thus manipulating the data.
Therefore, Call and Load are not data
manipulation instructions.

question:

reference instruction.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Memory reference instructions
Address part = 12 bits long.
Addressing mode = 1 bit.
Opcode = 3bits (from 000 to 110).
Register reference instructions
Addressing mode (1 bit) = 0.
Opcode (3bits) = 111. 
Input-output reference instructions
Addressing mode (1 bit) = 1.
Opcode (3bits) = 111. 
Hence, Options B and C do not represent
memory reference instructions; they are register
reference instructions.

question:
Arrange the following steps of the DHCP
(Dynamic Host Control Protocol) process in the
correct - sequence.
A. DHC PACK
B. DHCP DISCOVER
C. DHCP OFFER
D. DHCP REQUEST
E. Client receives IP configuration
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The correct sequence of steps in the DHCP
(Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) process
is:

DISCOVER message to find available DHCP
servers.

available IP address and other configuration
details.

REQUEST message, requesting the offered IP
address from one of the servers.

DHC PACK message, confirming the allocation of
the IP address and finalizing the process.
E. Client receives IP configuration: The client
receives the IP configuration, including IP
address, subnet mask, and gateway.

question:
In Java, which of the following statements is/are
True ?
S1 : The ‘final’ keyword applied to a class
definition prevents the class from being
extended through derivation.
S2 : A class can only inherit one class but can
implement multiple interfaces.
S3 : Java permits a class to replace the
implementation of a method that it has inherited.
It is called method overloading.

options.D: All of S1, S2 and S3

solution:
Option- A(S1 and S2 only)
Explanation:
S1: True. When the final  keyword is applied to
a class, it prevents that class from being
subclassed or extended. No class can extend a
final class.
S2: True. Java supports single inheritance for
classes (a class can only inherit from one
superclass), but it supports multiple inheritance
for interfaces (a class can implement more than
one interface).

question:
Which of the following statements is/are True ?
P : C programming language has a weak type
system with static types.
Q : Java programming language has a strong
type system with static types.
solution:
Option- C(Both P and Q)
Explanation:
P: C is frequently thought to have a weak type
system since it allows for greater freedom in type
conversions (such as casting between distinct
types) without tight checks. Although C is
statically typed (types are known at build time),
the flexibility of type conversions and pointer
arithmetic makes its type system less robust than
languages that rigidly enforce type safety.
Q: Java is recognized for its strong type system,
which requires stringent type checking. In Java,
variables must be defined with precise types,
and the compiler verifies type compliance. Java is
also statically typed, which means that type
checks are performed at compile time and before
the program is executed.
Thus, Q is also correct.

question:
Coupling is a measure of the strength of the
interconnections between software modules.
Which of the following are correct statements
with respect to module coupling ?
P : Common coupling occurs when one module
controls the flow of another module by passing it
information on what to do.
Q : In data coupling, the complete data structure
is passed from one module to another through
parameters.
R : Stamp coupling occurs when modules share a
composite data structure and use only parts of it.
      |       |

options.D: All of P, Q and R

solution:
Option- C(Q and R only)
Explanation:
Q: Data coupling refers to the scenario in which
modules communicate by transferring data
through parameters. When only the necessary
data is transmitted (rather than the entire
structure), the coupling is deemed low, which is
ideal.
R: Stamp coupling arises when modules share a
bigger data structure (for example, a record or
object) but only use a subset of it. This sort of
coupling is more limited than common coupling
yet less desirable than data coupling.

question:
A software design pattern often used to restrict
access to an object is :
solution:
Option- D(proxy)
Explanation: A proxy design pattern is commonly
used to limit or regulate access to an item. It
serves as a placeholder or substitute for another
object, controlling access to it. The proxy serves
as a middleman, executing specific tasks (such as
access control, logging, or lazy initialization)
before forwarding the request to the actual
object.

question:
A pushdown automata behaves like a Turing
machine when the number of auxiliary memory is
:
solution:
Option D is Correct
A Pushdown Automaton (PDA) is a type of
computational model that uses a stack as its
auxiliary memory. However, a Turing Machine
(TM) has unrestricted memory and is therefore
more powerful than a PDA. For a PDA to simulate
a Turing machine, it must have enough memory
to handle arbitrary computation.
1. PDA with One Stack: A PDA with 1 stack can
recognize only context-free languages (CFLs). It
is strictly less powerful than a Turing machine
because a single stack cannot emulate the
unrestricted memory of a Turing machine.
2. PDA with Two Stacks: A PDA with 2 stacks can
simulate a Turing machine:
One stack can be used to simulate the tape
of the Turing machine moving left.
The other stack can simulate the tape
moving right.
With 2 stacks, the PDA can recognize recursively
enumerable languages (RELs), the same as a
Turing machine.
3. PDA with More than 2 Stacks:
Adding more than 2 stacks does not provide
additional computational power beyond a Turing
machine.

question:
To obtain a string of n Terminals from a given
Chomsky normal form grammar, the number of
productions to be used is :
solution:
Option A is Correct
In CNF, every production rule is in one of the
following forms:
A→BC, where A,B, and C are non-terminal
symbols.
A→a, where A is a non-terminal and a is a
terminal.
Each production of the form A→BC generates
two new non-terminals, and each terminal a
corresponds to one final production.
1. To derive a string with n terminals, the CNF
grammar must produce exactly n terminals in the
final step.
2. Non-terminal productions: For n terminals, you
need n−1 intermediate non-terminal productions
to create the full binary structure that leads to n
leaves (terminals).
This is because every A→BC production reduces
the number of non-terminals by 1, and we start
with n−1 such reductions.
3. Terminal productions: Each of the n terminals
requires one terminal production (A→a).
Total Productions = (n−1) non-
terminal productions + n terminal productions =
2n−1.

internal and external:
Internal Fragmentation occurs when
allocated memory may have unused space

external fragmentation. It involves moving

contiguous blocks of free memory. This
process reduces fragmentation by
consolidating free space and making it
possible to allocate larger memory blocks to
processes that need them.
This statement is correct.

question:
In which of the following scheduling criteria,
context switching will never take place?
solution:
Non-preemptive SJF is a non-preemptive
scheduling algorithm.
Once a process starts executing, it runs to
completion without being interrupted.
No context switching occurs unless a process
completes or the CPU is idle and there are
new processes to execute.
A running process will not be preempted by
another process, so there is no context
switching between processes.

question:
In a Hierachical database, a hashing function is
used to locate the ________.
solution:
In hierarchical databases, the root of the
hierarchy is the starting point, from which all
other records (child records) are linked. In some
cases, a hashing function is used to locate the
root more efficiently, especially when the
structure is large or distributed. The root is the
most important entry in the hierarchical structure
because it serves as the entry point to all other
data.
Hashing for Root: A hashing function can be
applied to a key associated with the root record
to find its location in memory or storage more
quickly. Once the root is located, traversing the
hierarchical structure (children, grandchildren,
etc.) be done more efficiently.

question:
Relations produced from E - R Model will always
be in ________.
solution:
When relations are produced from an Entity-
Relationship (E-R) model, they are in 1NF
because:
1NF requires that all attributes contain only
atomic values (no multi-valued or composite
attributes). In the E-R model, entities are
represented as sets of attributes, and relations
derived from these entities must ensure that all
attributes are atomic by definition.
Example:
A relation will not have sets, lists, or arrays as
values in any attribute.
Multi-valued attributes are handled by creating
new relations (i.e., breaking them down into
simpler relations), ensuring atomic values in the
resulting tables.
When converting an E-R model to a relational
model, the relations (tables) will always satisfy
1NF, since the E-R model inherently ensures that
attributes are atomic.
Option A is correct.

The candidate keys are the minimal set of

It is not fully observable (i.e., the agent does

cannot predict the exact consequences of its
actions. This makes decision-making more
challenging.

heuristics  is available for a

others, which should we choose?
solution:
In heuristic search algorithms in Artificial
Intelligence (AI), if we have a collection of
admissible heuristics ( h, h, ......, h ) for a
problem and none of them dominates the others,
we should choose:
h(n) = max { h(n),........., h(n) }

informed estimate by taking the maximum value
among the available heuristics.

question:
Consider following sentences regarding A*, an
informed search strategy in Artificial Intelligence
(AI).
(a) A* expands all nodes with f(n) < C*.
(b) A* expands no nodes with f(n) /C*.
(c) Pruning is integral to A*.
Here, C* is the cost of the optimal solution path.
Which of the following is correct with respect to
the above statements?

options.A: Both statement (a) and statement (b) are true.
options.B: Both statement (a) and statement (c) are true.
options.C: Both statement (b) and statement (c) are true.
options.D: All the statements (a), (b) and (c) are true.

solution:
To solve this question, let's analyze each
statement about the A* algorithm:
(a)  A* expands all nodes with f(n) < C*: This is
true. A* will expand all nodes where the
estimated cost ( f(n) ) is less than the cost of the
optimal solution path ( C* ).
(b)  A* expands no nodes with f(n) ≥ C*: This is
also true. A* will not expand nodes where the
estimated cost ( f(n) ) is greater than or equal to
the cost of the optimal solution path ( C* ).
(c)  Pruning is integral to A*: This statement is not
necessarily true. While A can benefit from
pruning to improve efficiency, pruning is not an
inherent part of the A algorithm itself.
Based on this analysis, the correct answer is:
Both statement (a) and statement (b) are true.

used to give a better heuristic for a planning
problem.

schema in a planning problem results in a relaxed
problem.

solution:
(a) Planning Graph for Heuristic
A planning graph provides a better heuristic by
representing time steps as levels, starting from
the initial state. If a literal appears in the final
level, it is achievable; if not, it’s not possible to
achieve. The level at which a goal literal appears
can estimate the cost to achieve it, improving
heuristic accuracy.
(b) Dropping Negative Effects
Removing negative effects from action schemas
results in a relaxed problem, making planning
simpler. Negative effects impose restrictions that
increase time complexity, so eliminating them
increases possible actions, leading to a less
constrained and faster solution process.
So, option (B) is correct.

   The probability of A is the sum of p(i) for all

   Substituting back:

question:
Which of the following is an equivalence relation
on the set of all functions from Z to Z?
solution:
The correct option is D.
Equivalence relation: A relation is said to be an
equivalence relation if it is a reflexive, symmetric,
and transitive relation.
1. {(f,g) ∣ f(x)−g(x)=1 ∀ x ∈ Z}
It is not reflexive. As f(x) - f(x) =0 it is not 1. It is
also not transitive. So, it cannot be an
equivalence relation.
2. {(f,g) ∣  f(0) = g(0) or f(1) = g(1)}
This relation is not transitive.  for e.g. : Let (f, g),(g,
h) in R such that  f(0)=g(0)=1  and  g(1)=h(1)=2 
and  h(0)=4, f(1)=5. Here f is not related to h. Only
we have a relation given between f and g, g and
h. but not between f and h. So, it cannot be an
equivalence relation.
3. {(f,g) ∣  f(0) = g(1)  and f(1) = g(0)}
It is not always true f(0) = f(1) for the reflexive
case. So, it is not reflexive. Hence, no equivalence
relation.
4. {(f, g) ∣ f(x)−g(x)=k for some k ∈ Z}
It is a reflexive relation, considered constant as 0.
It is also symmetric because the difference will
be equal to a constant value. It is also transitive.
So, it is an equivalence relation.

at least one process can always complete and
release its resources.

n≤5

question:
In the context of software testing, which of the
following statements is/are NOT correct?
P : A minimal test set that achieves 100 % path
coverage will also achieve 100 % statement
coverage.
Q : A minimal test set that achieves 100 % path
coverage will generally detect more faults than
one that achieves 100 % statement coverage.
R : A minimal test set that achieves 100 %
statement coverage will generally detect more
faults than one that achieves100 % branch
coverage.
solution:
Statement P:
"A minimal test set that achieves 100% path
coverage will also achieve 100% statement
coverage."
Correct.
Path coverage is a stricter testing criterion than
statement coverage. Achieving 100% path
coverage ensures that every possible path
through the code is tested, which includes every
statement being executed at least once.
Q: A minimal test set that achieves 100% path
coverage will generally detect more faults than
one that achieves 100% statement coverage.
This statement is correct.
Path coverage tests multiple paths through the
program, which can reveal defects that arise from
specific combinations of statements. On the
other hand, statement coverage only ensures
that every statement is executed at least once,
but does not guarantee that all paths (and
potential interactions between statements) are
covered. As a result, achieving 100% path
coverage is generally more effective at detecting
faults than 100% statement coverage.
R: A minimal test set that achieves 100%
statement coverage will generally detect more
faults than one that achieves 100% branch
coverage.
This statement is NOT correct.
Branch coverage ensures that every possible
branch (decision point) in the program is taken at
least once, which typically provides more
thorough testing than statement coverage, which
only ensures that each statement is executed at
least once, regardless of the branches. In many
cases, branch coverage will detect more faults
because it takes into account the behavior of the
program under different decision outcomes,
whereas statement coverage does not consider
how combinations of statements might lead to
errors. Therefore, a test set achieving 100%
branch coverage will generally detect more faults
than one achieving 100% statement coverage.

question:
Which of the following is application of depth-
first search?

options.C:
Both topological sort and strongly connected
components
options.D:
Neither topological sort nor strongly
connected components

solution:
Option C is Correct
Depth-First Search (DFS) is a fundamental
algorithm used to explore graphs and has
numerous applications in graph theory. Among
its applications, Topological Sort and Strongly
Connected Components (SCCs) are key, and both
rely on DFS as their core algorithm. Let's analyze:
1. Topological Sort
Topological sort is a linear ordering of vertices in
a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) such that for
every directed edge u→v, vertex u comes before
v in the ordering. Role of DFS:
DFS is used to explore the graph and
determine the finishing times of each node.
Nodes are added to the stack in reverse order
of their finishing times during DFS traversal,
ensuring a valid topological order.
2. Strongly Connected Components (SCCs)
A strongly connected component of a directed
graph is a maximal subgraph where every vertex
is reachable from every other vertex in the same
component. Role of DFS:
DFS is used twice in Kosaraju's Algorithm or
Tarjan's Algorithm to find SCCs:
First DFS: Determines the finishing times of
vertices.
Second DFS (on the transposed graph):
Explores the graph in the reverse order of
finishing times to identify SCCs.
Both Topological Sort and Strongly Connected
Components are significant applications of DFS:
Topological Sort is used for linear ordering in a
DAG.
Strongly Connected Components help identify
cohesive substructures in directed graphs.
Hence, both rely on DFS for their computation.

A flow network is a directed graph G=(V,E)

satisfying specific properties.
P1: f(u,v)=−f(v,u) for all u,v ∈ V
This property ensures antisymmetry of the flow:
The flow from u to v is the negative of the
flow from v to u.
For example, if f(u,v)=5, then f(v,u)=−5.
This is a standard property in flow networks
because flow in the reverse direction cancels out
the original flow. Hence, P1 is True.

This property is called the flow conservation
property, At every vertex u, except the source
and sink, the total flow entering u equals the
total flow leaving u. This ensures that no flow is
"lost" or "created" at intermediate vertices. This
property is fundamental to flow networks and is
always true. Hence, P2 is also True.

question:
Consider the following statements about the
heap sort algorithm:
A. The MAX-HEAPIFY procedure which runs in
 time, is the key to maintaining the max
heap property
B. The BUILD-MAX-HEAP procedure, which runs
in  time, produces max-heap from an
unordered input array
C. The MAX-HEAP-INSERT, which runs in 
time, implements the insertion operation
D. The HEAP-INCREASE-KEY procedure runs in
 time, to set the key of a new node to
its correct value
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The correct answer is Option B ( A, C only ). 
A: Correct. The MAX-HEAPIFY procedure
ensures that the max-heap property is
maintained by comparing a node with its
children and making necessary swaps. It runs
in O(log n) time because it might need to
traverse from the node down to the leaf level
in the worst case.
B: Incorrect. The BUILD-MAX-HEAP
procedure transforms an unordered array into
a max-heap. While MAX-HEAPIFY runs in
 time, the BUILD-MAX-HEAP
process works on multiple nodes and, overall,
runs O(n) time, not O(log n) time.
C: Correct. The MAX-HEAP-INSERT operation
inserts a new element into the heap and then
"bubbles up" the element to restore the heap
property. This process takes O(log n) time
because it may need to move the element up
the tree, which has a height of log n.
D: Incorrect. The HEAP-INCREASE-KEY
procedure adjusts the value of a node and
restores the max-heap property by moving
the node upward. This operation only needs
O(log n) time since it only traverses up the
tree, not O(n log n).

question:
Consider the following statements:
A. A database design is in BCNF if each member
of the set of relation schemas that constitutes
the design is in BCNF
B. A BCNF schema can have transitive
dependency
C. It is always possible to obtain a 3 NF design
without sacrificing a lossless join
D. There are multivalued dependencies in 4 NF
solution:
The correct answer is A, C and D only.
A. A database design is in BCNF if each
member of the set of relation schemas that
constitutes the design is in BCNF. This statement
is true because the definition of BCNF ( Boyce-
code Normal Form ) states that for every
dependency X -> Y in a relation. X must be a
super key and this applies at schema level (a set
of attributes ) in a relation. If all relation schemas
are in BCNF, the database design can said to be
in BCNF.
B. A BCNF schema can have transitive
dependency. This statement is false because
according to the definition of BCNF for every
dependency X -> Y in a relation. X must be a
super key and this disallows transitive
dependencies ( i.e. if X->Y and Y->Z then X->Z )
which would imply that there is a non-superkey
attribute that determines another attribute.
C. It is always possible to obtain a 3 NF design
without sacrificing a lossless join. This
statement is true because normalizing a
database schema to 3NF can be done without
losing the ability to perform lossless join by
ensuring that whenever any functional
dependency X->Y causes a violation, the
decomposition of relation includes X in all
decomposed relation.
D. There are multivalued dependencies in 4
NF. This statement is true because 4NF ( Fourth
Normal Form ) is designed to handle multivalued
dependencies because multivalued dependency
always require at least three attributes because it
consists of at least two attributes that are
dependent on a third. 
Bases on the explanation statements A, C and D
are correct.

knowledge because it focuses on user
experience rather than logical capabilities, unlike
inferential adequacy, efficiency properties which
are essential for accurate reasoning processes.

question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled
as Assertion A and the other is labelled as
Reason R .
A virtual memory system uses first-in first-out
page replacement policy and allocates a fixed
number of frames to a process
Assertion A: Increasing number of page frames
allocated to a process sometimes increases the
page fault rate.
Reason R: Some programs do not exhibit locality
of reference.
In the light of the above statements, choose the
correct answer from the options given below.

options.A:
Both A and R are true and R is the correct
explanation of A
options.B:
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the
correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

solution:
The correct answer is option B. Both A and R are
true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
First In First Out Page Replacement Algorithm :
In this algorithm, the operating system keeps
track of all pages in the memory in a queue,
oldest page is in the front of the queue. When a
page needs to be replaced page in the front of
the queue is selected for removal. 
FIFO Page replacement algorithms suffer from
Belady’s anomaly : 
Belady’s anomaly states that it is possible to
have more page faults when increasing the
number of page frames. 
Statement P: Increasing the number of page
frames allocated to a process sometimes
increases the page fault rate. 
Correct, as FIFO page replacement algorithm
suffers from belady’s anomaly which states the
above statement. 
Statement Q: Some programs do not exhibit a
locality of reference. Correct, Locality often
occurs because code contains loops that tend to
reference arrays or other data structures by
indices. So we can write a program that does not
contain a loop and does not exhibit locality of
reference. 
So, both statements P and Q are correct but Q is
not the reason for P as Belady’s Anomaly occurs
for some specific patterns of page references.

operator in the context of genetic algorithms.

question:
Which is not the component of the natural
language understanding process?
solution:
Option - D (Meaning Analysis)
Meaning analysis is not the component of the
natural language understanding process. 
Natural Language Understanding Process: The
umbrella of natural language processing in
artificial intelligence includes natural language
understanding and interpretation. Numerous
uses for it exist, including digital assistants,
chatbots, as and automatic translation services.
There are five components/ phases of NLP are as:
Step 1: Lexical Analysis and
Morphological: Lexical analysis is the first stage
of NLP in which  the source code is scanned as a
character stream and transformed into
meaningful lexemes. It breaks the text into
words, phrases, and paragraphs.
Step 2: Syntatic Analysis: Syntactic analysis
checks grammar, arranges words, and illustrates
word relationships.
Step 3: Semantic Analysis:Semantic analysis is
focused on the representation of meaning. It
primarily concentrates on a word, phrase, or
sentence's literal meaning.
Step 4: Discourse Integration: Discourse
integration draws meaning from the sentences
that come before it as well as from those that
follow.
Step 5: Pragmatic Analysis: The fifth and final
stage of NLP is pragmatic. It assists you in
determining the desired outcome by using a set
of guidelines typical of cooperative talks.

10,000 transactions x 24,000 bits/transaction =
240 × 10 bits
We must convert this amount because the
enquiry asks for throughput in megabits per
second.
60 seconds is one minute, so the throughput is
240
Throughput =  240 x 10 bits/minute / 60
seconds/minute = 4 megabits/second

question:
Given below are two statements:
Which of the following concurrency control
protocol ensures both conflict serializability and
freedom from deadlock?
Statement I: Two phase locking
Statement II: Timestamp ordering
In the light of the above statements, choose the
most appropriate answer from the options given
below:

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B:
Both Statement I and Statement II are
incorrect
options.C:
Statement I is correct but Statement II is
incorrect
options.D:
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is
correct

solution:
Statement I: Two-phase locking (2PL)
Two-phase locking ensures conflict
serializability by dividing the transaction into
two phases: the growing phase (where locks
are acquired) and the shrinking phase (where
locks are released). However, it does not
guarantee freedom from deadlock.
Statement II: Timestamp ordering
Timestamp ordering ensures conflict
serializability by ordering transactions based
on their timestamps. It also guarantees
freedom from deadlock because transactions
are ordered chronologically, preventing
circular wait conditions.
Given this analysis, the most appropriate answer
is:
D. Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is
correct.

question:
Find the sum of all four digit numbers formed
using the digits 1,2,4 and 6 .
solution:
Step-by-Step Explanation:
Step 1: Determine the total number of possible
numbers
Since we are using 4 digits (1, 2, 4, and 6) and
arranging them into four-digit numbers, the total
number of such numbers is:
4!=24 (4 factorial means there are 24 different
ways to arrange 4 digits).
So, we can make 24 numbers in total.
Step 2: Analyze the contribution of each digit
Every digit (1, 2, 4, and 6) will appear equally in
each position (thousands, hundreds, tens, ones).
Since we are making 24 numbers, and there are 4
positions, each digit will appear:
24/4=6 times in each position.
For example, the digit 1 will appear in the
thousands place 6 times, the hundreds place 6
times, and so on.
Step 3: Calculating each digit contributes to the
total sum
When a digit appears in the thousands place, its
value is multiplied by 1000.
When a digit appears in the hundreds place, its
value is multiplied by 100.
When a digit appears in the tens place, its value
is multiplied by 10.
When a digit appears in the ones place, its value
stays the same.
So, the contribution from each digit to the final
sum is based on the place it occupies.
The sum of the digits: The sum of the digits 1, 2,
4, and 6 is:
1+2+4+6=13
This total sum (13) is the basis for calculating how
much each place contributes to the overall total.
Step 4: Calculating the contribution to each
place:
Since each digit appears 6 times in each place
(thousands, hundreds, tens, ones), the
contribution for each place is:
6×(1000+100+10+1) = 6×1111=6666
Now, multiply this by the sum of the digits:
13×6666 = 86,658
Final Answer:
The total sum of all four-digit numbers formed
using the digits 1, 2, 4, and 6 is 86,658.
Thus, the correct answer is Option A: 86,658.

question:
Which is not a basic approach to the problem of
conflict resolution in a production system?

options.A:
Assigning a preference based on the rule that
matched
options.B:
Assigning a preference based the object that
matched
options.C:
Assigning a preference based on the action
that the matched rule would perform
options.D:
Assigning a preference based on the action
that the matched object would perform

solution:
Option A: Rule-based preference
Correct: This method is effective because the
system resolves conflicts by giving priority to the
rule that is triggered first. It guarantees that the
most relevant rule is applied when several rules
would fit.
Option B: Object-based preference
Correct: This method is good when particular
objects hold greater priority. The system
organizes and assigns priority to rules based on
the involved object, which is beneficial when
objects possess specific characteristics that
require focus.
Option C: Action-based (rule) preference
Correct: It is reasonable to prioritize according to
the action a rule will execute, particularly when
the system must assess the implications of
various actions. The outcomes of the action
influence which rule is deemed more critical.
Option D: Action-based (object) preference
Incorrect: Objects do not carry out actions; rules
do. Therefore, assigning priority based on an
"object's action" lacks logic and is not applicable
in production systems.
Summary:
A, B, and C are valid approaches because they
prioritize based on the rules.
Option D is not correct because objects do not
carry out actions. Therefore, it is incorrect to
prioritize based on an action performed by an
object.

question:
Consider the following statements.
A. The identity is unique in any monoid.
B. A monoid is a group if there exists inverse of
each element of monoid.
C. Semi group has closure, associative and
identity properties.
D. Quasi group has closure property.
solution:
Option A: The identity is unique in any monoid.
True: In any monoid, we have at most one
identity element. This characteristic allows
everything else in the set to stay the same when
combined with it.
Example: Consider the set of non-negative
integers N={0,1,2,3,...} under the operation of
addition (+).
The identity element in this monoid is 0 because,
for any a ∈  N, we have: a+0=0+a=a
So, the identity element (0) is unique.
Option B: A monoid is a group if there exists an
inverse of each element of the monoid.
True: A monoid satisfies the group property as
well, apart from having an identity element, any
element has its inverse associated with it.
Example: Consider the set of integers Z under
addition.
The identity element is 0.
Each element a ∈  Z has an inverse, which is -a,
since: a+(-a)=(-a)+a=0
Therefore, Z under addition forms a group
because every element has an inverse.
Option C: A semigroup has closure, associative,
and identity properties.
False: A semigroup doesn't need to have an
identity property. It does not require an
identifying component. 
Example: The set of positive integers Z+={1,2,3,...}
under multiplication forms a semigroup.
Closure: Multiplying two positive integers always
results in another positive integer.
Associativity: For any a,b,c ∈ Z+, we have:
(a ∗ b) ∗ c=a ∗ (b ∗ c)
However, there is no identity element in this
semigroup because there is no number in Z+ such
that a ∗ e=e ∗ a=a for all a ∈ Z+.
Option D: A quasigroup has closure property.
True: A quasigroup follows the closure property
—this means that any operation upon elements
from the set outputs another element from the
given set.
Example: The set Z5  = {0,1,2,3,4} under the
operation of modular addition forms a
quasigroup.
Closure: For any a,b ∈ Z5, the result of a+b mod 5
is still within Z5. For example: 3 + 4 mod 5= 2. This
set is a quasigroup because it satisfies closure.
Option A:
A, B, and D are correct.

question: Shift-Reduce conflicts are resolved by :
solution:
Shift-reduce conflicts occur in parser generators
(like in parser combinators or parser generators
for languages like LR parsers) when the parser
encounters a situation where it can either shift
(move to the next state and expect more input)
or reduce (apply a production rule and reduce
the current stack of symbols).
To resolve shift-reduce conflicts, parser
generators typically use the following
mechanisms:
Option D) Associativity and Precedence: This is
the most common method to resolve shift-
reduce conflicts. Operators in programming
languages often have associativity (whether
operations are evaluated left-to-right or right-to-
left) and precedence (which operation takes
precedence over another). By specifying the
associativity and precedence of operators in the
grammar, the parser can decide whether to shift
or reduce based on the current operator and the
one at the top of the stack.
Associativity: Determines the direction (left or
right) in which operations of the same
precedence are evaluated. For example, in many
programming languages, addition and
subtraction are left-associative.
Precedence: Determines the order of operations
when multiple operators are present. For
example, multiplication has higher precedence
than addition.
Option A) Left Recursion: Left recursion is a
parsing technique where the left-most non-
terminal symbol in a production rule appears
again as the first symbol in the right-hand side of
the rule. Left recursion can sometimes lead to
conflicts, but it is not typically used to resolve
shift-reduce conflicts directly.
Option B) Left Factoring: Left factoring is a
technique used to refactor grammar rules to
eliminate common prefixes. This technique can
help in reducing the number of conflicts but is
not directly used to resolve shift-reduce conflicts.
Option C) Ambiguity: Ambiguity in grammar can
lead to conflicts, including shift-reduce conflicts.
Resolving ambiguity involves restructuring the
grammar to remove multiple interpretations of
the same input string, but this does not directly
resolve shift-reduce conflicts.
So option D is the correct answer.

together and run as a group. The programmers
leave their programs with the operator and the
operator then sorts the programs with similar
requirements into batches.
B. A time-sharing processor's time which is
shared among multiple users simultaneously is
termed as time-sharing.

Batch Systems and Time-Sharing Systems is that
in the case of Multiprogrammed batch systems,

whereas in Time-Sharing Systems, the objective

copy of the program code can be shared by

code cannot modify itself and the local data for
each user must be stored separately. In a shared
system, reentrancy allows more efficient use of
main memory: One copy of the program code is
kept in the main memory, but more than one
application can call the procedure. So D matches

question:

process?
solution:

handled during the semantic analysis phase,
where the compiler checks if types are
compatible and converts them if necessary.

the lexical analysis phase (often called scanning),
which precedes semantic analysis. It involves
breaking down the source code into tokens
(keywords, identifiers, literals, etc.) for further
processing.
Option C) Loop optimization: This is part of the
optimization phase of compilation, where the
compiler analyzes loops and optimizes them for
performance. 
Option D) Data flow Analysis- To efficiently
optimize the code compiler collect all the
information about the program and distribute
this information to each block of the flow graph.
This process is known as data-flow graph analysis
which is done at code optimization phase.
So option A is the correct answer.

generated and stored on a different set of the
disk.

message into blocks, calculating redundant
parity data for each block based on the message
contents, and transmitting the blocks with parity.

question:
A computer system with a cache access time of
100 ns, a main memory access time of 1100 ns,
and a hit ratio of 0.9 , then the average access
time would be :
solution:
To calculate the average memory access time
given the cache access time, main memory
access time, and hit ratio, we use the following
formula:
Average Access Time (AAT) = Hit ratio×Cache
access time+(1−Hit ratio)×Main memory access
time
Given:
Cache access time = 100 ns
Main memory access time = 1100 ns
Hit ratio = 0.9
Now, substitute these values into the formula:
Average Access Time (AAT) = 0.9×100 ns +
0.1×1100 ns
Calculate each term: 0.9×100 ns = 90 ns
0.1×1100 ns = 110 ns
Now, sum these values to get the average access
time:
AAT = 90 ns + 110 ns
AAT = 200 ns
Therefore, the average access time is 200 ns
So option A is the correct answer.

question:
Arrange in appropriate order, the construction of
a finite automata :
A. Minimum State DFA
B. Regular Expression
C. NFA-
D. Problem Statement
E. DFA
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The correct order for constructing a finite
automaton progresses as follows:
Problem Statement (D): Understand the problem
that the automaton needs to solve, including the
language it should accept or recognize.
Regular Expression (B): Express the language that
the automaton should recognize using a regular
expression. Regular expressions are a concise
way to describe patterns in strings.
NFA-  (C): Construct a nondeterministic finite
automaton (NFA) based on the regular
expression. NFAs allow multiple transitions from
a state on the same input symbol and can have ε -
transitions (epsilon transitions).
NFA- to DFA Conversion: Convert the NFA to a
deterministic finite automaton (DFA). This
conversion eliminates ε -transitions and
nondeterminism, resulting in a DFA.
Minimum State DFA (A): Minimize the DFA
obtained from the previous step. Minimization
reduces the number of states while preserving
the language recognized by the automaton.
So option B is the correct answer.
