question:
The techniques used to handle the phantom
problem are
A. Time stamping
B. Index locking
C. Predicate locking
D. Execution indexing
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
solution:
|       |   


UGC	NET
Option A) The basic timestamp ordering protocol
(BASIC T/O) allows reads and writes on database
objects without using locks. Instead, every
database object X is tagged with a timestamp of
the last transaction that successfully performed a
read (denoted as R-TS(X)) or write (denoted as
W-TS(X)) on that object. The DBMS then checks
these timestamps for every operation. If a
transaction tries to access an object in a way that
violates the timestamp order, the transaction is
aborted and restarted
For dynamic databases in which transactions
perform insertions, updates, and deletions time
stamping will not be sufficient. 
The phantom phenomenon arises when two
transactions logically conflict even though they
do not lock a common data item. In a database,
the phantom problem is a scenario where a
transaction reads a set of rows from the
database that match a certain condition, and
when the same transaction attempts to read the
rows again (using the same condition), it
discovers additional rows that weren't there
previously. These new rows are known as
'phantoms'.
Approaches to Address the Phantom Problem:
1. Re-Execute Scans: Transactions may re-run
queries at commit time to check for different
results, indicating missed changes due to new or
deleted records.
2. Predicate Locking: This involves acquiring locks
based on the predicates of the queries, ensuring
that any data that satisfies the predicate cannot
be modified by other transactions.A predicate
lock in database systems is a type of lock that
prevents the modification of all data rows that
satisfy a specific condition, thus ensuring data
integrity when multiple transactions access the
same data simultaneously.
3. Index Locking: Utilizing index keys to protect
ranges of data, preventing phantoms by ensuring
that no new data can fall within the locked
ranges. After an index range is locked, no other
transaction can insert, update, or delete any row
within this range until the transaction that holds
the lock completes. In this way, index locking
ensures the consistent state of a transaction,
resolving the phantom problem.
Option D) Indexing often refers to the process of
creating and maintaining data that allow for
efficient access to elements based on some key
or index. For dynamic database concurrency
problems like phantom problem indexing is not
alone sufficient.
So option B is the correct answer.

question:
IP is responsible for ________ communication
while TCP is responsible for ________
communication.
solution:
IP (Internet Protocol) is responsible for host-to-
host communication, while TCP (Transmission
Control Protocol) is responsible for process-to-
process communication.
Here's a breakdown of what each term means in
this context:
IP (Internet Protocol):
IP is a fundamental protocol in the Internet
protocol suite (TCP/IP).
It provides the addressing and routing
mechanism that enables packets to be routed
across networks.
IP handles the addressing and routing of
packets between hosts (computers or devices)
on a network.
Its primary responsibility is to deliver packets
from the source host to the destination host
based on IP addresses.
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol):
TCP is a protocol that operates at a higher level
than IP in the TCP/IP stack.
It provides reliable, ordered, and error-
checked delivery of a stream of bytes
between applications running on hosts
communicating over an IP network.
It manages process-to-process communication
by establishing a connection between the
sender and receiver, managing data flow,
handling acknowledgments, and
retransmitting lost packets if necessary.
The data link layer is responsible for the node-to-
node delivery of the message. The main function
of this layer is to make sure data transfer is error-
free from one node to another, over the physical
layer. The socket is primarily a concept used in
the transport layer of the Internet protocol suite
or session layer of the OSI model. 
So option D is the correct answer.

question:
In windows scheduling, which of the following
option is correct ?
solution:
Windows uses a priority-based scheduling
algorithm to manage processes running on the
system. This prioritization helps determine which
processes get access to CPU time and in what
order. Windows categorizes priorities into two
main types: real-time priorities and non-real-time
priorities.
Real-time priorities are used for critical system
tasks that require immediate attention and are
typically reserved for system-level processes.
They have a higher priority than non-real-time
priorities.
Non-real-time priorities are used for user-level
processes and applications. These priorities
are further subdivided into 16 levels.
Here’s how the 16 non-real-time priority levels are
structured:
They range from 0 (lowest) to 15 (highest).
Each level represents a different priority at
which a process can run relative to other non-
real-time processes.
Higher priority levels (closer to 15) indicate
more urgency and readiness to execute,
whereas lower levels (closer to 0) indicate less
urgency and lower priority.
These priorities are dynamic and can change
based on various factors such as process
behavior, resource availability, and system
load.
The scheduling algorithm in Windows adjusts
these priorities to ensure fair access to CPU
resources while prioritizing processes that
need more immediate attention.
So option D is the correct answer.

memory, which contrasts with isolated I/O where

specifically relate to the addressing scheme.

readiness or acknowledgment but is not directly
related to memory and I/O address separation.

current activities to handle a specific event. It is
not directly related to the distinction between
memory and I/O addresses.

question:
Which of the following are true for a complete
binary tree?
A. It has always odd number of vertices.
B. With i internal vertices, it has i+1 leaves.
C. With l leaves, it has 2l-1 vertices.
D. With 2 n-1 vertices, it has n leaves.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
solution:
Explanation:
The following statements are True for a complete
binary Tree:
A. It is always an odd number of vertices. This is
True. For n>1, a full binary tree must have an odd
number of nodes (since each node has either 0
or 2 children, and we start with 1 root node). So, n
should be odd.
B. With i internal vertices, it has i+1 leaves. True. In
a complete binary tree, the number of internal
vertices i is equal to the number of leaves l plus
one:l=i+1
This relationship holds because each internal
vertex has exactly two children (except possibly
the last level of the tree), and each leaf
corresponds to a node that does not have any
children.
C. With l leaves, it has 2l−1 vertices.
True. The total number of vertices v in a
complete binary tree with l leaves is given
by:v=2l−1
D. With 2n−1 vertices, it has n leaves. True. For a
complete binary tree with n leaves, the total
number of vertices v is v=2n−1. This relationship
holds because every complete binary tree with n
leaves has 2n−1 vertices in total.
So option D is the correct answer.

question:
Which of the following are White box Testing?
A. Path Testing
B. Loop Testing
C. Regression Testing
D. Non-functional Testing
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
solution:
White box testing refers to a testing technique
where the internal structure, design, and
implementation of the software under test are
known to the tester. Let's analyze each option to
determine which ones are considered white box
testing techniques:
A. Path Testing:
Path testing is a white box testing technique
where test cases are designed to execute all
possible paths in a software application's source
code.
It requires knowledge of the internal structure
and logic of the code to ensure that every path is
tested.
B. Loop Testing:
Loop testing is a white box testing technique that
focuses on testing the functionality of loops
within the code.
Test cases are designed based on the structure
of loops and their boundaries, requiring
knowledge of the loop structure and logic.
C. Regression Testing:
Regression testing is not specifically a white box
testing technique. It is a type of testing that
ensures previously developed and tested
software still performs correctly after a change
or addition.
It does not require knowledge of the internal
structure of the software but focuses on the
overall functionality.
D. Non-functional Testing:
Non-functional testing is a type of testing that
verifies the non-functional aspects of the
software such as performance, reliability,
usability, etc.
It is not specifically a white box testing technique
as it does not require knowledge of the internal
structure of the software.
So option A is the correct answer.

question:
Techniques for performing I/O :
A. Programmed I/O
B. Interrupt-driven I/O
C. Rotational I/O
D. Direct memory access
E. Channelized I/O
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
solution:
A. Programmed I/O:
In programmed I/O, the CPU controls data
transfer between external devices and memory
directly using I/O instructions. This method
involves the CPU actively waiting for each I/O
operation to complete before proceeding, which
can be inefficient for large data transfers.
B. Interrupt-driven I/O:
Interrupt-driven I/O allows the CPU to handle
other tasks while waiting for I/O operations to
complete. When an I/O operation finishes, the
device sends an interrupt signal to the CPU,
prompting it to handle the completed operation.
This approach reduces CPU idle time and
improves overall system efficiency.
D. Direct Memory Access (DMA):
DMA allows external devices to transfer data
directly to or from memory without CPU
intervention. A DMA controller manages the data
transfer, freeing the CPU to perform other
tasks.This method significantly reduces CPU
overhead and speeds up data transfer rates
between devices and memory.
C. Rotational I/O:
Rotational I/O is not a standard term for
describing I/O techniques in general computing
contexts. It refers to specific operations in disk
drives where data is read or written as the disk
rotates, but it's not commonly listed as a general
      |       |   


UGC	NET
I/O technique.
E. Channelized I/O:
Channelized I/O involves using specialized
hardware channels or controllers to manage I/O
operations independently of the CPU. It's
commonly used in mainframe and high-
performance computing environments to offload
I/O processing from the CPU, but it's less
commonly categorized as a fundamental I/O
technique compared to programmed I/O,
interrupt-driven I/O, and DMA.
So option B is the correct answer.

question:
For the software quality assurance, which of the
following is correct?
A. Execution of code
B. No execution of code
C. Preventive technique
D. A corrective technique
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
solution:
Option A)  Execution of code: This refers to
running the actual software code to test its
functionality, performance, and other attributes.
This is a fundamental part of testing in SQA.
Option B) No execution of code: This refers to
techniques such as static analysis, code reviews,
inspections, and walkthroughs, where the focus is
on examining the code or design without actually
running the software. So this is included in the
software quality assurance process. These
techniques aim to identify issues and defects
early in the development lifecycle before the
software is executed.
Option C) Preventive technique: This refers to
techniques and activities that aim to prevent
defects from occurring in the software. This
includes activities such as requirements analysis,
design reviews, code reviews, and the use of
coding standards and guidelines which include
software quality assurance processes. 
Option D) A corrective technique: This refers to
techniques applied after defects or issues have
been identified during testing or after
deployment. Examples include debugging,
rework, and patching to fix bugs that were
discovered.
So option B is the correct answer.

question:
In a token ring network the transmission speed is
10 and the propagation speed is 200 m / μ s . The
1-bit delay in this network is equivalent to
________________
solution:
The correct answer is Option A ( 20 m ).
To determine the 1-bit delay in a token ring
network, we need to consider the transmission
speed and propagation speed.
Transmission speed (T) = 10 bits per second
(bps)
Transmission delay for 1 bit = 1 / T = 1/10 = 0.1 μ s
Propagation speed (P) = 200 meters per
microsecond (m/ μ s)             
1-bit delay = ( Transmission delay for 1 bit ) x (
Propagation speed)
                 = [(1 bit) / T ]× P
                 = [(1 bit) / (10 bps)] × (200 m/ μ s)
                 = (0.1 μ s) x 200 m/ μ s
                = 20 m
Therefore, the 1-bit delay in this network is
equivalent to 20 meters.

question:
Consider a relation schema R=(U, V, W, X, Y, Z), on
which the following functional dependencies
hold
{U→V, VW→X, Y→W; X→U}
The candidate keys of R are :
solution:
Step 1: Identify which attributes are dependent
on others.
U→V means if we know U, we can determine V.
VW→X means knowing V and W, we can
determine X.
Y→W means knowing Y, we can determine W.
X→U means knowing X, we can determine U.
Step 2: Find the closure of attribute
combinations to determine candidate keys.
Closure of UY:
U→V, so UY determines V.
Y→W, so UY determines W.
VW→X, so UY determines X.
X→U, so UY already determines U (nothing new).
Thus, UY+={U,V,W,X,Y}, covering all attributes
except Z.
Closure of VY:
Y→W, so VY determines W.
VW→X, so VY determines X.
X→U, so VY determines U. Thus, VY+={U,V,W,X,Y},
covering all attributes except Z.
Closure of XY:
X→U, so XY determines U.
U→V, so XY determines V.
Y→W, so XY determines W. Thus, XY+={U,V,W,X,Y},
covering all attributes except Z.
Step 3: Evaluate the candidate key options.
To cover all attributes, including Z, we need to
extend the combinations:
UY, VY, and XY determine all attributes except Z.
Therefore, adding Z to these combinations will
cover all attributes.
Thus, the correct candidate keys are UYZ, VYZ,
and XYZ.
The correct option is D: UYZ,VYZ,XYZ.

remains unchanged while the datagram is sent.

question:
A CPU has a 5-stage pipeline with the following
stages Fetch (F), Decode (D), Execute (E), Memory
(M) and Write-back (W). Each stage takes one
clock cycle to complete. Assume there are no
pipeline stalls and the pipeline is initially empty.
How many clock cycles are required to complete
the execution of 10 instructions?
solution:
In a pipelined CPU with 5 stages (Fetch, Decode,
Execute, Memory, Write-back), each stage
processes one instruction per clock cycle, but
instructions can overlap in the pipeline.
The time to complete n instructions in a pipelined
processor is given by:
total clock cycles = number of stages  + n -1
Here:
Number of stages = 5 (F, D, E, M, W)
Number of instructions n=10
So, the total clock cycles required are:
5 +10-1 = 14
Thus, 14 clock cycles are needed to complete the
execution of 10 instructions.
correct option is B).14

solution:

Only ).  
A sorting algorithm is stable if it maintains the
relative order of equal elements.
(A) Quick Sort is an unstable sorting algorithm
because it does not preserve the relative order of
equal elements.
(B) Bubble Sort is a stable algorithm it ensures
that two objects with equal keys appear in the
sorted output in same order they appear in the
input.
(C) Insertion Sort is also a stable algorithm that
maintains the relative order of equal elements in
the sorted output.
(D) Merge Sort is also a stable algorithm that
uses the divide and conquer technique to
recursively divide the input into two halves and
merge them back together and maintains the
relative order of equal elements.
(E) Shell Sort is an unstable sorting algorithm
because it does not guarantee that the relative
order of equal elements will be maintained in the
sorted output.

connection request.

the information present in the TCP segment
header that is sent by B to A ?

options.A:
SYN bit =1, SEQ number =S+1, ACK bit =0, ACK
number =R, FiN bit =0
options.B:
SYN bit =0, SEQ number =R, ACK bit =1, ACK
number =S+1, FiN bit =0
options.C:
SYN bit =1, SEQ number =R, ACK bit =1, ACK
number =S+1, FiN bit =0

SYN bit =1, SEQ number = R, ACK bit =1, ACK
number =S, FiN bit =0

solution:

Explanation: The following actions are taken
during the TCP three-way handshake in order to
create a connection:
1.  Sending a TCP segment, host A contains:
     - SEQ number = S
     - SYN bit = 1
     - Since this is the first connection request, the
ACK bit is set to 0.
     - The ACK number is not relevant.
2.  After receiving the SYN segment from host
A, host B answers with a segment of its own. In
return, Host  B is going to:
     -  As part of its own SYN segment, set SYN bit
to 1 to acknowledge the request.
     -  Use its own sequence number R.
     -  To show that it is recognizing A's SYN
request, set the ACK bit to 1.
     -  The ACK number will be set to S + 1
      The final  TCP segment header information
sent by B to A will be: SYN bit =1, SEQ number
=R, ACK bit =1, ACK number =S+1, FiN bit =0

Declaration and Initialization:
An array named arr is defined, containing the
elements {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.
A pointer p is initialized to point to the first
element of the array (i.e., p points to arr[0], which
holds the value 1).
First Print Statement (printf("%d", *p++);):
The expression *p dereferences the pointer p,
which at this moment points to arr[0], yielding
the value 1.
Following this, the p++ operation shifts the
pointer to the next element in the array (now
pointing to arr[1], which is 2).
Consequently, the output of this statement is 1.
Second Print Statement (printf("%d", *(p + 1));):
After executing the first print statement, p now
references arr[1], which is 2.
The expression *(p + 1) retrieves the value located
one position ahead of the current pointer,
leading it to point to arr[2].
The value at arr[2] is 3, so *(p + 1) evaluates to 3.
Thus, the output of this statement is 3.

The ascending order of these grammars is
Regular < Context-Free < Context-Sensitive <
Unrestricted
The ascending order of the Chomsky Hierarchy is
based on the expressive power of the grammars,
which refers to the types of languages they can
generate or describe. The levels are ordered
according to the complexity of the languages
they define and the power of the computational
models (automata) required to recognize those
languages.
Type 3 (Regular Grammars): Can only generate
the simplest languages, known as regular
languages. These languages have a very
restricted structure, such as strings that can be
recognized by a finite automaton (like patterns in
regular expressions).
Type 2 (Context-Free Grammars): Can generate
more complex languages, including many
programming languages, like balanced
parentheses, that cannot be handled by regular
grammars. These are recognized by a pushdown
automaton.
Type 1 (Context-Sensitive Grammars): Can
describe even more complex languages, where
the structure of the language depends on the
context in which the symbols appear. Recognized
by a linear bounded automaton.
Type 0 (Unrestricted Grammars): Can describe
the most complex and general languages,
including all computable languages. These are
recognized by a Turing machine, which has no
restrictions on memory or structure.

question:
Arrange the following steps in the correct order
to solve the Knapsack problem using Dynamic
Programming.
(A) Define the base case when the capacity is
zero (0) or no items are left to consider
(B) Compute the maximum value that can be
obtained using items up to the i-th item and a
knapsack capacity of 0
(C) Identify subproblems and their dependencies
based on items weights and values
(D) Initialize a table to store results of
subproblems
(E) Iterate through each item and each possible
Capacity to fill the table
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
(A) (C), (D), (A), (E), (B)
(B) (D), (C),
solution:
Explanation:
Base Case: If the knapsack's capacity is zero or
no items are left, the maximum value is zero. This
serves as the initial condition.
Identify Subproblems: Break down the problem
by considering each item's inclusion or exclusion.
The goal is to find the maximum value for
different capacities and item combinations.
Initialize Table: Create a table where rows
represent items and columns represent knapsack
capacities. This table will store the results of
subproblems.
Iterate: For each item and capacity, decide
whether to include the item. If included, add the
item's value to the best solution for the remaining
capacity. Update the table with the maximum
value.
Compute Maximum Value: Once the table is
filled, the value at the bottom-right cell gives the
maximum value for the full capacity of the
knapsack.
The Final Answer is: (A), (C), (D), (E), (B)

Total cycles =  64 operations * 5 cycles /
operations = 320 cycles

asked.

The Banker's Algorithm is a critical deadlock
avoidance method in operating systems,
designed to facilitate resource allocation without
causing deadlock. It operates by maintaining
information about the maximum resources. Each
process may require, the current allocated
resources and the available resources in the
system. The algorithm checks each resource
request to determine, if granting it would leave
the system in a safe state, meaning that there is
always a sequence in which all processes can
complete their execution without getting stuck
due to resource unavailability. Each process must
specify its maximum demand for each resource
type before it starts execution. When a process
requests additional resources, the algorithm
checks if granting the request will keep the
system in a safe state. If so, the resources are
allocated otherwise the process must wait until
its request can be safely fulfilled.

question:
Which of the following is NOT a
requirement for Banker's algorithm to
grant a resource request ?

options.A:

options.B:

solution:
Option - D ( The process must be the only one
requesting resources.)
Explanation:
A: The requested resources must be available:
Before approving a request, the Banker's
algorithm verifies that the resources are now
available. Should they not be accessible, the
request will not be fulfilled.
B: The system must be in a safe state after
granting the request:This is an essential
prerequisite. The Banker's algorithm makes sure
that the system can continue distribute resources
to all processes so that they can all complete,
even after approving a resource request.
Granting the request could result in a deadlock if
the system is not safe.
 C: The request must not exceed the maximum
resources the process can request: This is also
necessary. To avoid possible resource depletion,
the Banker's algorithm verifies that the present
request does not surpass the maximum number

of resources that each process is allowed to seek.
D: The process must be the only one requesting
resources: This is not necessary. The Banker's
algorithm is capable of managing several
concurrent resource requests from different
programs. It is made to make sure that resource
allocation may be controlled in a way that keeps
the system safe and prevents deadlock even
when there are several processes running at
once.

question:
Which data structure does the Banker's
Algorithm use to maintain the state of
available, maximum and allocated
resources ?
solution:
Option - D ( Matrices and Vectors )
Explanation -
A: Priority Queue: This method concentrates on
process scheduling according to priority and is
not appropriate for managing resource status.
B: Hash table: In the context of the Banker's
Algorithm, it does not well illustrate the
connections between various operations and the
resources they require.
C: Wait-for-Graph: This graph is primarily used
to detect deadlocks; it does not keep track of the
states of allocated, maximum, and available
resources.
D: Matrices and Vectors -  Banker's Algorithm
makes use of:
  - Available Vector: Monitors resources that are
accessible.
  - Maximum Matrix: Shows the highest level of
resources required for every process.
  - Allocated Matrix: Displays the resources that
are currently assigned to various processes.

question:
What is the significance of the Banker's
algorithm in terms of resource
management?

options.A:
It enures that all processes can finish
their execution without deadlock.
options.B:
It eliminates the need for processes to
request resources.
options.C:
It accelerates the execution of critical
sections in processes.
options.D:
It minimizes the number of context
switches between processes.

solution:
Option - A (It enures that all processes can
finish their execution without deadlock.)
One of the main purposes of the Banker's
Algorithm is to guarantee that no process can
stall out during its execution. It employs a safety
check to make sure that resource distribution
does not result in a deadlock, enabling the safe
completion of every process.

question:
What is the primary goal of the Banker's
Algorithm?

options.B:
To prevent processes from requesting
resources
options.C: To detect and recover from deadlocks

solution:
Option- A  ( To allocate resources optimally )
Explanation: 
A: To allocate resources optimally  - The main
objective is to distribute resources so as to
prevent deadlocks and guarantee that every
process has a chance to finish.
B: To prevent processes from requesting
resources  - This is untrue; the algorithm permits
requests for resources but controls them to avoid
deadlocks.
C: To detect and recover from deadlocks - The
Banker's Algorithm aids in deadlock prevention,
but it does not concentrate on deadlock
detection or breakage.
D: To maximize CPU utilization - The Banker's
Algorithm prioritizes safe resource management
over outright CPU usage optimization, even if
effective resource allocation might result in
higher CPU utilization.

question:
What information is used to determine if
a resource request can be granted ?

options.A:
Available resources and current
allocation of each process
options.C:
Number of processes waiting for
resources

solution:
Option - A ( Available resources and current
allocation of each process )
Explanation: 
A: Available resources and current allocation of
each process  - The Banker's Algorithm uses this
data to assess whether approving a resource
request maintains the system in a safe state.
B: CPU utilization of each process - The Banker's
Algorithm bases its resource allocation decisions
on demand and availability of resources; CPU
usage is not taken into consideration.
C: Number of processes waiting for  resources -
Although useful for context, this figure by itself
does not indicate whether a particular resource
request may be approved in a safe manner.
D: Arrival time of each process - The Banker's
Algorithm does not take arrival time into
account; instead, it concentrates on the
allocation and availability of resources at the
moment, not the scheduling or timing of
processes.

question:
Once the process is allocated CPU and executing
which of the following events could not occur?
A. The process could issue an I/O request and
then be placed in the Ready Queue
B. The process could create new subprocesses &
wait for the termination of the subprocesses
C. The time slice of the process expires and it
may join the waiting queue
D. The process is forcibly removed from the CPU
and is put in the Waiting queue due to arrival of
an interrupt
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Option A: "The process could issue an I/O
request and then be placed in the Ready
Queue"
Incorrect Statement
If a process issues an I/O request, it is moved
to the Waiting (or Blocked) queue, not Ready
queue.
Ready Queue is for processes waiting for CPU
without any I/O pending.
Option B: "The process could create new
subprocesses & wait for the termination of the
subprocesses"
Correct Statement
This is valid; a process can use fork() or
create() system call and then perform
wait() to block itself until child processes
finish.
Option C:"The time slice of the process expires
and it may join the waiting queue"
Incorrect Statement
If the time slice expires, the process is
preempted and sent to the Ready queue, not
the Waiting queue.
Waiting queue is only for I/O or other
blocking events.
Option D: "The process is forcibly removed from
the CPU and is put in the Waiting queue due to
arrival of an interrupt"
Incorrect Statement
Interrupts may cause preemption, but the
process is sent to the Ready queue, unless the
process itself makes a blocking call.
An interrupt alone does not move a process
to the Waiting queue.
Correct Answer: Option D) A, C and D Only

question:
Consider the following interrupt protection levels
in Linux, and arrange them in the increasing
order of their priorities.
A. User-Mode Programs (Preemptible)
B. Bottom Half Interrupt Handlers
C. Top Half Interrupt Handlers
D. Kernel System Service Routines (Preemptible)
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
In Linux interrupt handling, there is a clear
hierarchy of priority levels:
1. User Mode Programs (A) – Have the lowest
priority, can be preempted at any time by
kernel or interrupts.
2. Kernel System Service Routines (D) – Run in
kernel mode, but are still preemptible by
interrupt handlers.
3. Bottom Half Interrupt Handlers (B) – These
are deferred interrupt handlers (e.g., softirqs,
tasklets); they run after the top half
completes.
4. Top Half Interrupt Handlers (C) – Highest
priority. Executed immediately when an
interrupt occurs. Cannot be preempted by
anything except another (higher) interrupt.
Correct Answer: Option D) A → D → B → C

question:
Which of the following technique is used for
Clipping?
solution:
Sutherland–Cohen is a classic line clipping
algorithm used in computer graphics.
It is designed to clip line segments against a
rectangular clipping window.
The algorithm uses region codes (called
outcodes) for the endpoints of the line.
These outcodes help determine:
If the line is completely inside the clipping
window → accept it.
If the line is completely outside → reject it.
If the line is partially inside → calculate the
intersection points and clip the line
accordingly.
Correct Answer: C) Sutherland-Cohen

question:
Identify the correct statement(s) from the
followings with respect to Spinlock Semaphores
A. The name refers to busy waiting semaphores.
B. They are not useful when the locks are to be
held for a short duration of time.
C. It may require multiple context switches when
a process waits on a lock.
D. They are often employed on Uniprocessor
systems.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
A. The name refers to busy waiting semaphores
→ Correct. 
Spinlocks use busy-waiting (i.e., they
continuously check a condition in a loop while
holding CPU cycles), hence the term
“spinning.”
They don’t block or sleep the process.
B. They are not useful when the locks are to be
held for a short duration of time → Incorrect
Spinlocks are useful for short-duration locks,
because avoiding context switches in such
cases is more efficient than sleeping/waking.
C. It may require multiple context switches
when a process waits on a lock → Incorrect
Spinlocks avoid context switches; that's why
they're used for short wait times.
This statement applies more to blocking
semaphores, not spinlocks.
D. They are often employed on Uniprocessor
systems → Incorrect
On Uniprocessor systems, spinlocks are
inefficient, because spinning wastes CPU
cycles and no other process can release the
lock while it's spinning.
Spinlocks are better suited to multiprocessor
systems.
Correct Answer: Option A Only

question:
Only legal pointer operations:
A. pointer + number  pointer
B. pointer - number number
C. pointer + pointer   pointer
D. pointer - pointer   pointer
E. pointer - pointer   number
Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
solution:
Legal Pointer Operations in C:
A. pointer + number → pointer: This is a valid
operation. Adding an integer to a pointer
moves the pointer by that many units of the
size of the data type it points to. For example,
if you have int *p; and you do p + 5;, p will
point to the memory location 5 ints past its
original location. The result is another pointer.
B. pointer - number → number: This is also
not a valid operation. Subtracting an integer
from a pointer moves it backward in memory.
The result is another pointer.
C. pointer + pointer → pointer: This is not a
legal operation in C. We cannot add two
pointers together.
D. pointer - pointer → pointer: This is not a
legal operation in C. While we can subtract
two pointers (see E), the result is not a pointer.
E. pointer - pointer → number: This is a valid
operation. Subtracting one pointer from
another (if they point to elements within the
same array or block of memory) yields the
number of elements between them. The result
is an integer type (specifically, ptrdiff_t).

question:
Arrange the following in the increasing order of
coupling from lowest coupling to highest
coupling.
A. Common Coupling
B. Stamp Coupling
C. Control Coupling
D. External Coupling
E. Content Coupling
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Coupling from lowest (best) to highest (worst):
1. Stamp Coupling: When modules share a
complex data structure (like a record or
object), but only part of it is used. This is
relatively low coupling.
2. Control Coupling: One module controls the
behavior of another by passing control
information (e.g., flags). This increases
dependency.
3. External Coupling: Modules share information
through an external format or protocol (e.g.,
file formats, communication protocol).
Stronger than control coupling.
4. Common Coupling: Multiple modules share
global variables. Changes in one module can
impact all others. High level of coupling.
5. Content Coupling: One module directly
modifies or uses internal data or code of
another module. This is the highest and worst
form of coupling.
So, the increasing order of coupling is:
Stamp Coupling → Control Coupling → External
Coupling → Common Coupling → Content
Coupling
i.e. B → C → D → A → E
Correct Option: C) B, C, D, A, E

serializable, if it is conflict-equivalent to some
serial schedule.

serializable if it is view-equivalent to some serial
schedule.
C. A schedule is said to be serial, if instructions of

interleaved with each other.

serializable also but vice-versa may not be true.

A — True

serial schedule.
B — True
This is the definition of view serializability.
View serializable ⇔  view equivalent to a serial
schedule.

A serial schedule means:
All instructions of one transaction are

Every conflict-serializable schedule is also

Because conflict-serializability ⊆  view-

Some view-serializable schedules are not

This statement is incorrect. STRIPS is actually

question:
Arrange the following types of testing in the
order they are usually performed in the software
Development life cycle.
A. Integration testing
B. Unit testing
C. System Testing
D. Acceptance Testing
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The typical order of testing in the software
development lifecycle (SDLC) is as follows:
B. Unit Testing: This is the first level of testing
and focuses on testing individual components or
modules of the software in isolation.
A. Integration Testing: This is conducted after
unit testing and verifies the interactions and data
flow between integrated modules.
C. System Testing: This comes after integration
testing and evaluates the behavior of the entire
system as a whole against the specified
requirements, including both functional and non-
functional aspects.
D. Acceptance Testing: This is the final phase of
testing, typically performed by end-users or
clients to verify if the software meets their needs
and expectations before deployment.
This order follows a logical progression, starting
with testing individual components and gradually
building up to testing the entire system from the
user's perspective. 
 
Correct Answer: Option B) B, A, C, D

question:
The correct sequence of constructing Huffman
tree is
A. Repeat until root formed
B. Create leaf nodes
C. Build priority queue
D. Combine lowest frequency nodes
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
The correct sequence for constructing a Huffman
tree is as follows:
B. Create leaf nodes: Start by creating a leaf
node for each unique character in the input data,
along with its frequency.
C. Build priority queue: Insert all the created
leaf nodes into a priority queue (or min-heap)
based on their frequencies. Nodes with lower
frequencies are given higher priority.
D. Combine lowest frequency
nodes: Repeatedly remove the two nodes with
the lowest frequencies from the priority queue.
Create a new internal node where these two
nodes are its left and right children, and the new
node's frequency is the sum of their frequencies.
A. Repeat until root formed: Continue repeating
step D, reinserting the newly formed internal
nodes into the priority queue, until only one
node remains in the queue. This remaining node
is the root of the Huffman tree, and the
construction is complete.
Correct Answer: Option C) B, C, D, A

Let m and n are positive integers. Then
(A) If n neq 1, then m<m n.
(B) If k is composite, then k=m n where 1<m, n>k
(C) If mn =1, then m =1 and n =1.
(D) If k is composite, then k=m n where 1<m, n<k
Which of the following is correct:
(A)
solution:
(A) If n ≠ 1, then m < mn.
Since m and n are positive integers, and n ≠ 1, it
means n must be greater than or equal to 2 (n ≥
2).
Multiplying both sides of the inequality m < mn
by 1/m (which is positive since m is a positive
      |       |

integer) gives 1 < n.
This is true if n ≠ 1 and n is a positive integer.
Therefore, statement (A) is correct.
 
(B) If k is composite, then k = mn where 1 < m, n
> k.
A composite number k can be written as a
product of two positive integers m and n, where 1
< m < k and 1 < n < k.
The condition "1 < m, n > k" implies that both m
and n are greater than k, which is impossible if k
= mn and m, n are positive.
For example, if k = 6, then m and n could be 2
and 3. Here, 1 < 2 < 6 and 1 < 3 < 6.
So, statement (B) is incorrect.
 
(C) If mn = 1, then m = 1 and n = 1.
Since m and n are positive integers, the only way
their product can be 1 is if both m and n are 1.
If m were greater than 1, then mn would be
greater than n, and if n were greater than 1, then
mn would be greater than m. For mn to be 1, both
m and n must be 1.
Therefore, statement (C) is correct.
 
(D) If k is composite, then k = mn where 1 < m, n
< k.
This is the standard definition of a composite
number. A positive integer k is composite if it can
be written as the product of two smaller positive
integers m and n, both greater than 1 and less
than k.
Therefore, statement (D) is correct.

To calculate the Effective Memory Access Time
(EMAT) in a system with a single-level page table
and a TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer), we use
the formula:

First, to fetch the page table entry (150 ns).
Second, to fetch the data (150 ns).
TLB search adds 15 ns. So, Total time =
15+150+150=315 ns
Calculating EMAT, EMAT = (Hit Rate × Hit Time) +
(Miss Rate × Miss Time)
EMAT = (0.8×165) + (0.2×315) = 132 + 63 = 195ns.

names and their attributes, such as data type,
size, and memory location.

and functions during compilation.

variables and functions. During semantic analysis,

redundant error reporting.

question:
In the context of 3D Computer graphics, which of
the following statements is/are correct?
(A) Under perspective projection, each set of
parallel lines in the object do not stay parallel in
the image (except those that are parallel to the
viewplane to start with).
(B) Applying a perspective transformation in the
graphics pipeline to a vertex involves dividing by
its ' (z) ' coordinate.
(C) Perspective transformation is a linear
transformation.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(A) (A) and (B) only
(B)
solution:
Perspective Projection:
Simulates the way the human eye perceives
depth, causing objects farther from the viewer to
appear smaller.
A key property is that lines that are parallel in the
3D world may appear to converge in the image,
forming a vanishing point, except for lines
parallel to the view plane.
Perspective Transformation:
Transforms 3D points into a 2D perspective view.
This transformation involves dividing the
coordinates by the depth (z-coordinate) to
achieve the perspective effect.
Linearity of Perspective Transformation:
Perspective transformation is not a linear
transformation because dividing by the z-
coordinate introduces a non-linear component.
Linear transformations maintain straight-line
relationships, while perspective projection does
not.
Option A is correct.

question:
Software reliability is described with respect to
(A) Execution Time
(B) Calendar Time
(C) Clock Time
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(A) (A) and (B) only
(B) (B) and (C) only
(C)
solution:
Software reliability refers to the probability of a
software system operating without failure under
specified conditions for a specified period. It is
measured using various time-related factors that
affect the system’s operation.
Execution Time (A):
This means the actual time the software is in use
or running.
Reliability is measured during execution because
it directly reflects the operational performance
of the software.
Calendar Time (B):
This represents the elapsed time from
deployment or release, including downtime or
periods when the software is not actively in use.
While it can indicate reliability trends over a long
term (e.g., maintenance issues or failure
frequency), it is not a primary factor for real-time
reliability.
Clock Time (C):
It refers to real-world time during which the
software operates, typically including idle times
or when the software is not executing actively.
Reliability during clock time is also relevant,
especially for systems that depend on uptime
and availability.
Option C is correct.

question:
Which among the following statement(s) is (are)
true?
(A) A hash function takes a message of arbitrary
length and generates a fixed length code.
(B) A hash function takes a message of fixed
length and generates a code of variable length.
(C) A hash function may give same hash value for
distinct messages.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(A)
solution:
Statement A
"A hash function takes a message of arbitrary
length and generates a fixed-length code."
This statement is true as A hash function is
designed to accept input messages of any
length. Whether the message is a single
character or an entire book, the hash function
can process it. Despite the varying input lengths,
a hash function always produces an output (also
known as a hash value or digest) of a fixed size.
For example:
MD5 Hash Function: Always produces a
128-bit hash value.
SHA-256 Hash Function: Always produces a
256-bit hash value.
This property is crucial for tasks like data
integrity verification and cryptography, where
consistent output sizes are needed for
comparison and further processing.
Hence, Statement A accurately describes how
hash functions work.
Statement C
"A hash function may give the same hash value
for distinct messages."
This statement is true since A hash collision
occurs when two different input messages
produce the same hash output.

question:
Which of the following cloud concept/s is/are
related to pooling and sharing of resources?
(A) Virtual Memory
(B) Service
(C) Virtualization
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(A) (C) only
(B)
solution:
Option A is Correct
Cloud computing relies on the pooling and
sharing of resources to provide scalable and
efficient services. Let’s analyze each concept:
(A) Virtual Memory:
Virtual memory is a technique used in operating
systems to extend physical memory by using disk
space. While it's resource-efficient for local
machines, it is not directly related to cloud
resource pooling and sharing. Hence, It is Not
related to the concept.
(B) Service:
"Service" in cloud computing (e.g., SaaS, PaaS,
IaaS) represents a deliverable over the internet,
but it doesn’t inherently manage resource
pooling or sharing. Hence, It is Not directly
related to the concept.
(C) Virtualization:
Virtualization is the key enabler of cloud
computing, allowing multiple virtual resources
(e.g., VMs) to share the same physical hardware.
This is directly related to pooling and sharing of
resources. Hence, it is Directly Related to the
Concept.
Only Statement C is Directly Related.

question:
Post office protocol (POP) is a message access
protocol which is used to extract message for
client. In this regard, which of the following are
true?
(A) POP has two modes, Delete mode and keep
(B) In Delete mode, mail is deleted from mail box
after each retrival
(C) In Delete mode, mail is deleted from mail box
before each retrieval
(D) In keep mode, mail is deleted before retrival
(E) In keep mode, mail remains in mail box after
retrival
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(A) (A) and (B) only
(B) (A), (D) and (E) only
(C)
solution:
Option D is Correct
Post Office Protocol (POP) is a simple message
access protocol used by email clients to retrieve
messages from a mail server.
(A) POP has two modes, Delete mode and Keep
mode.
This Statement is True as POP provides two main
modes of operation: Delete mode (where emails
are removed after retrieval) and Keep mode
(where emails remain on the server after
retrieval).
(B) In Delete mode, mail is deleted from the
mailbox after each retrieval.
This Statement is True as In Delete mode, the
server removes emails from the mailbox after
they are successfully retrieved by the client.
(C) In Delete mode, mail is deleted from the
mailbox before each retrieval.
This Statement is False as Emails are not deleted
before retrieval in Delete mode; they are deleted
after retrieval.
(D) In Keep mode, mail is deleted before retrieval.
This Statement is False as In Keep mode, emails
are not deleted before retrieval; they remain on
the server after retrieval.
(E) In Keep mode, mail remains in the mailbox
after retrieval.
This Statement is True as The Keep mode ensures
that emails are left intact on the server even
after retrieval.

question:

protected network from the outside network.
Firewalls can filter the packets on the basis of

Since, A firewall is a network security device that
monitors and controls incoming and outgoing
network traffic based on predetermined security
rules. Firewalls can filter packets based on
various criteria:

Firewalls can block or allow packets originating
from specific source IP addresses.
2. Destination IP Address (B):
Firewalls can block or allow packets heading to
specific destination IP addresses.

Firewalls can filter packets based on the TCP
source port, which indicates the application on
the source device sending the data.

Firewalls can filter packets based on the UDP
source port, which indicates the application on
the source device sending the data.
5. TCP Destination Port (E):
Firewalls can filter packets based on the TCP
destination port, which indicates the application
on the destination device.

question:
Which of the following statements are true?
(A) Minimax search is breadth-first; it processes
all the nodes at a level before moving to a node
in next level.
(B) The effectiveness of the alpha-beta pruning is
highly dependent on the order in which the
states are examined.
(C) The alpha-beta search algorithm computes
the same optimal moves as minimax algorithm.
(D) Optimal play in games of imperfact
information does not require reasoning about the
current and future belief states of each player.
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(A) (A) and (C) only
(B)
solution:
Option C is Correct
Examining each Statement we get,
(A) Minimax search is breadth-first; it processes
all the nodes at a level before moving to a node
in the next level.
It is False as Minimax search is depth-first
because it recursively explores child nodes until
reaching terminal states, then backtracks. It does
not process all nodes at one level before
proceeding.
(B) The effectiveness of the alpha-beta pruning is
highly dependent on the order in which the
states are examined.
It is True as Alpha-beta pruning is more effective
when better moves (closer to optimal) are
examined earlier, as it allows more pruning.
(C) The alpha-beta search algorithm computes
the same optimal moves as minimax algorithm.
It is True as Alpha-beta search is an optimization
of minimax, providing the same results with
potentially fewer node evaluations.
(D) Optimal play in games of imperfect
information does not require reasoning about the
current and future belief states of each player.
It is False as In games of imperfect information,
reasoning about belief states (what the other
players know or believe) is critical for optimal
play.

question:
Let us assume a person climbing the stairs can
take one stair or two stairs at a time. How many
ways can this person climb a flight of eight stairs?
solution:
Let f(n) be the number of ways to reach the n
stair. The recurrence relation is:
f(n) = f(n−1)+f(n−2)
If the person takes 1 step, they have f(n−1)
ways to reach the remaining stairs.
If the person takes 2 steps, they have f(n−2)
ways to reach the remaining stairs.
The base cases are:
f(1) = 1: There is 1 way to reach the first stair.
f(2) = 2: There are 2 ways to reach the second
stair.
Calculate f(n) for n=3 to n=8:
1. f(3) = f(2)+f(1)=2+1=3
2. f(4) = f(3)+f(2)=3+2=5
3. f(5) = f(4)+f(3)=5+3=8
4. f(6) = f(5)+f(4)=8+5=13
5. f(7) = f(6)+f(5)=13+8=21
6. f(8) = f(7)+f(6)=21+13=34
So, the number of ways to climb a flight of 8
stairs is 34.
Option D is correct.

solution:

topological sorting, and analyzing graph
structures.

v (for a source node S) if every path from S to v
passes through u. In simpler terms,u is
unavoidable on any route from S to v. This
concept is commonly used in program
optimization and analysis of control flow graphs.
A reducible graph is a control flow graph (CFG)
where loops are well-structured and can be
simplified into standard forms.
The Final Answers are A, B, and C.

number of vertices with an odd degree is even.
This is a well-known result in graph theory, often
referred to as the Handshaking Lemma. The
lemma states that the sum of the degrees of all
vertices in a graph is equal to twice the number
of edges. Since each edge contributes 2 to the
total degree count, the sum of the degrees is
even. The vertices with odd degrees must pair up

number of vertices with an odd degree must be
even.

sum of the degrees of all vertices is even. This is
also true, due to the Handshaking Lemma. The
sum of the degrees is equal to twice the number
of edges, which is always even.

question:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: Breadth‐First Search is optimal when
all the step costs are equal whereas uniform‐cost
search is optimal with any step‐cost.
Statement II: When all the step costs are same
uniform‐cost search expends more nodes at
depth d than the Breadth‐First Search.
In light of the above statements, choose the
correct answer from the options given below

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

solution:
(True) Statement I: "Breadth-First Search is
optimal when all the step costs are equal
whereas uniform-cost search is optimal with any
step-cost."
Breadth-First Search (BFS): This search
algorithm is optimal when all step costs are
equal because it explores all nodes at the
present depth before moving on to nodes at
the next depth level. This means that it will
find the shortest path in terms of the number
of edges when all edges have the same cost.
Uniform-Cost Search: This search algorithm is
optimal for any step cost, including cases
where step costs vary. It expands the least-
cost node first, ensuring that it always finds
the least-cost path to the goal.
Statement II is TRUE because at depth d, when
we implement breadth first search with same
cost at all nodes, it will have to search lesser
nodes but uniform cost search will always check
for the lowest cumulative cost, hence, will
expend more nodes than BFS.

Statement A: "Greedy best‐first search is not
optimal but is often efficient."
This statement is true. The greedy best-first
search uses a heuristic to guide its search, which
can make it efficient in terms of time, but it does
not guarantee an optimal solution.
Statement B: "A is complete and optimal
provided h(n) is admissible or consistent."*
This statement is true. A* search is complete (it
will find a solution if one exists) and optimal (it
will find the least-cost path) if the heuristic ( h(n)
) is admissible (never overestimates the true cost
to reach the goal) or consistent (satisfies the
triangle inequality).
Statement C: "Recursive best‐first search is
efficient in terms of time complexity but poor in
terms of space complexity."
This statement is false. Recursive best-first search
is actually efficient in terms of space complexity
because it uses linear space (proportional to the
depth of the search tree). However, it can be
inefficient in terms of time complexity because it
may revisit nodes multiple times.
Statement D: "h(n) = 0 is an admissible heuristic
for the 8‐puzzle."
This statement is true. A heuristic that always
returns 0 is admissible because it never
overestimates the cost to reach the goal (it
estimates it as 0, which is less than or equal to
the actual cost).

question:
Given a fixed‐length record file that is ordered
on the key field. The file needs   disk blocks to
store   number of records. Find the average
access time needed to access any record of the
given file using binary search.
solution:
The correct answer is option D.
To find the average access time needed to access
any record in a fixed-length record file that is
ordered on the key field using binary search, we
can follow these steps:
Accessing Disk Blocks: In a binary search, the
maximum number of comparisons needed to find
a record in a sorted list of size ( R ) is ( log(R) ).
However, since we are dealing with disk blocks,
we need to consider how many disk accesses are
required.
Disk Blocks: Given that the file is stored in ( B )
disk blocks, and assuming that each block can
hold multiple records, we need to determine how
many records are in each block. If ( R ) is the total
number of records and ( B ) is the number of disk
blocks, the average number of records per block
is ( R/B ).
Average Access Time: In the worst case, binary
search will access ( log(B) ) disk blocks. However,
since we are interested in the average access
time, we consider that for each level of the
binary search, we might access a block. The
average number of disk block accesses will be
the sum of disk block accesses across all levels of
the search.
 
The average access time ( T ) for accessing any
record = log(B) + 1
The "+1" is for the initial access to the first block.
Thus, the average access time needed to access
any record of the given file using binary search is
approximately: O(log(B))

question:
The cache coherence problem can be solved
A. by having multiport memory
B. allow only nonshared data to be stored in
cache
C. using a snoopy cache controller
D. using memory interleaving
Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
solution:
Option B is Correct
(A) Multiport Memory:
Multiport memory facilitates multiple processors
accessing the same memory simultaneously.
However, it does not directly address cache
coherence, as it does not ensure that the cached
copies remain consistent across processors.
Hence, Statement A is Incorrect.
(B) Allow Only Nonshared Data to Be Stored in
Cache:
By caching only nonshared data, the cache
coherence problem is avoided entirely. However,
this is not a scalable solution in systems where
shared data is common, but it is technically a
valid solution. Hence, Statement B is Correct.
(C) Using a Snoopy Cache Controller:
A snoopy cache controller uses coherence
protocols (e.g., MESI) to monitor and ensure
consistency of cached data by broadcasting
updates or invalidations over the shared bus. This
is an efficient and widely-used solution for the
cache coherence problem. Hence, Statement C is
Correct.
(D) Using Memory Interleaving:
Memory interleaving improves memory access
speed by splitting memory into banks for parallel
access. It does not address cache coherence, as it
focuses on access optimization rather than
consistency. Hence, Statement D is Incorrect.

question:

protocols allows the transfer of multimedia?
solution:

MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) is
an extension of the basic email protocol that
allows the transmission of multimedia content,
such as images, audio, video, and non-ASCII text
(e.g., attachments). MIME does not replace
existing protocols like SMTP but works with them
to encode and decode multimedia data. MIME
extends the capability of email systems to
support non-textual data and multiple types of
attachments. Without MIME, emails are limited to
plain text.
Whereas, IMAP (Internet Message Access
Protocol) is Used to retrieve and manage emails
stored on a mail server. It does not handle
multimedia.

sending of plain text email but does not
inherently support multimedia. MIME is used
alongside SMTP for multimedia support.
POP3 (Post Office Protocol 3) is Used to retrieve
emails from a server, but it does not include
multimedia handling capabilities.

consisting of an odd number of inverted bits is:
solution:
Option A is Correct
Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) detects
transmission errors by using a generator
polynomial G(x). It ensures certain properties to
detect specific types of errors. A polynomial G(x)
can detect all errors with an odd number of
inverted bits if and only if (x+1) is a factor of G(x).

(x+1) corresponds to binary 11, which ensures that
the CRC calculation detects all odd-parity errors.

factor, it guarantees that the resulting checksum
is sensitive to any error with an odd number of
bit flips, as such errors will always generate a
non-zero remainder.

δ (q,a,z)={(q,11z)}: On input a and stack top

to q.
δ (q,a,1)={(q,111)}: On input a and stack top
1, push two more 1's onto the stack
(effectively pushing three 1's for each a in q 
).
δ (q,b,1)={(q, λ )}: On input b and stack top 1,
pop the stack.
δ (q, λ ,z)={(q,z)}: If the stack has returned to
z in q with no remaining input, move to the
accepting state q .
Step-by-Step Analysis of the Language
1. Processing a's in State q :
When the NPDA reads an a in state q  with
z on the stack, it transitions to q  and
pushes two 1's onto the stack.
For each subsequent a read in q  with 1 on
the stack, the NPDA pushes two additional
1's onto the stack.
Therefore, for every a in the input, the stack
gains two 1's.
This setup implies that after reading 2n a's, the
stack will have n×2=2n 1's.
1. Processing b's in State q :
When the NPDA reads a b in q with 1 on
top of the stack, it pops the stack.
Therefore, each b in the input corresponds
to one pop operation on the stack.
2. Balancing the a's and b's:
For the NPDA to reach the accepting state
q  (while consuming all input), the number
of b's must match the number of pops
required to empty the stack of the 1's
pushed by the a's.
Since each a contributes two 1's to the
stack, there must be twice as many b's as
a's in any accepted string.
Therefore, the language accepted by the
NPDA is:L={a b∣ n≥0}

question:
Which mode is a block cipher implementation as
a self synchronizing stream cipher?
solution:
Cipher Feedback (CFB) Mode enables a block
cipher to function as a self-synchronizing
stream cipher.
In CFB mode, the previous ciphertext block is
encrypted rather than directly encrypting the
plaintext.
The encrypted output of the previous block is
then XORed with the current plaintext block
to generate the new ciphertext block.
This process allows CFB mode to behave
similarly to a stream cipher, with the added
benefit of self-synchronization.

question:
Which of the following algorithm design
approach is used in Quick sort algorithm?
solution:
The Quick Sort algorithm uses the Divide and
Conquer approach to sort an array
These are follow these step solve problem:
Step 1: Divide: Select a pivot and partition the
array around it, placing smaller elements to the
left and larger elements to the right.
Step 2: Conquer: Recursively apply the same
steps to the left and right sub-arrays.
Step 3: Combine: No explicit combination is
needed; partitions are sorted in place.

question:
Consider the following statements of
approximation algorithm :
Statement I: Vertex-cover is a polynomial time 2-
approximation algorithm.
Statement II: TSP-tour is a polynomial time 3-
approximation algorithm for travelling salesman
problem with the triangle inequality.
Which of the following is correct?

options.A: Statement I true and Statement II false
options.B: Statement I and Statement II true
options.C: Statement I false and Statement II true
options.D: Statement I and Statement II false

solution:
Statement I: Vertex-cover is a polynomial time 2-
approximation algorithm.
True: The Vertex Cover problem has a  2-
approximation algorithm that operates in
polynomial time. In this algorithm, we find a
vertex cover within twice the optimal size, it is
called a 2-approximation algorithm.
Statement II: TSP-tour is a polynomial time 3-
approximation algorithm for the Travelling
Salesman Problem (TSP) with the triangle
inequality.
False: For the Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP)
with the triangle inequality, there exists a 2-
approximation algorithm, not a 3-approximation.
The triangle inequality allows for a 2-
approximation approach (often using algorithms
based on the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) or
Christofides' algorithm).
Option A is the correct answer.

question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Composite attributes cannot be
divided into smaller subparts.
Statement II: Complex attribute is formed by
nesting composite attributes and multivalued
attributes in an arbitrary way.
Statement III: A derived attribute is an attribute
whose values are computed from other attribute.

solution:
Statement I: Composite attributes cannot be

solution:

question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: LALR parser is more powerful than
canonical LR Parser.
Statement II : SLR parser is more powerful than
LALR
Which of the following is correct?

options.A: Statement I true and Statement II false
options.B: Statement I false and Statement II true
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II false
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II true

solution:
Statement I: LALR parser is more powerful than
canonical LR parser
False: Canonical LR parsers (also known as
LR(1) parsers) are more powerful than LALR
parsers because they can handle a larger class
of grammars. Canonical LR parsers have
separate states for each lookahead, which
makes them more powerful than LALR parsers,
which combine states with the same core but
different lookaheads to reduce the number of
states.
Statement II: SLR parser is more powerful than
LALR
False: LALR parsers are more powerful than
SLR parsers. LALR parsers handle a larger set
of grammars than SLR parsers because they
use lookahead symbols more effectively. SLR
parsers use a simple lookahead mechanism,
which makes them less powerful than LALR
parsers.
Option C is correct.

question:
Consider the following statements about Context
Free Language (CFL) :
Statement I: CFL is closed under homomorphism.
Statement II: CFL is closed under complement.
Which of the following is correct?

options.A: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
options.B: Statement II is true and Statement I is false
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.D: Neither Statement I nor Statement II is true

solution:
Statement I: CFL is closed under homomorphism
True: A homomorphism is a function that maps
symbols from one alphabet to strings over
another alphabet. Context-free languages are
closed under homomorphism. This means that
if L is a CFL, applying a homomorphism to L
will result in another CFL.
Statement II: CFL is closed under complement
False: Context-free languages are not closed
under complement. This means that if L is a
CFL, the complement of L may not necessarily
be a CFL. This is a property of CFLs.
Option A is correct.

question:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled
as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : A load-and-go assembler avoids
the overhead of writing the object program out
and reading it back in.
Reason ( R ) : This can be done with either one-
pass or two pass assembler.
In the light of the above statements, choose the
correct answer from the options given below :

options.A:
Both ( A ) and ( R ) are true and ( R ) is the
correct explanation of ( A )
options.B:
Both ( A ) and ( R ) are true but ( R ) is NOT
the correct explanation of ( A )
options.D: (A) is false but ( R ) is true

solution:
The correct answer is option A.
Load-and-go assemblers generate their object
code in memory for intermediate execution. No
object program is written out, no loader is
needed.
Assertion (A): A load-and-go assembler avoids
the overhead of writing the object program out
and reading it back in.
This statement is true. A load-and-go assembler
directly loads the program into memory and
executes it without creating an intermediate
object file, thus eliminating the overhead
associated with writing to and reading from
storage.
Reason (R): This can be done with either a one-
pass or two-pass assembler.
This statement is also true. Both one-pass and
two-pass assemblers can be designed as load-
and-go. One-pass assemblers also avoid the
overhead of an additional pass over the source
program.
